Everyone said that the Master was a man of such renowned virtue in the present age that he ought not to have committed such an act. When it was confirmed that the Master had indeed made no other statement from the beginning, he was consequently sentenced to penal servitude in Shaanxi.
Upon hearing this, he wept with great remorse and pleaded for mercy. The Master said, "If my original intention had been such as you say, I would rather die ten thousand deaths than do it."
The Master did not look back, and upon reaching Baoying, he said to his attendants, "My retribution-body is quite different from usual;
it seems my end is near. That night they stayed at Ningguo Temple. Its abbot, Master Zongxu Liao, had been an old acquaintance of the Master, and they greeted each other with great joy.
The Master said, "I have found a place for my bones to be entrusted. That night they conversed together and ate and drank as usual. At dawn the following day—
Suddenly, with his hands joined in *añjali* and sitting upright, he passed away in profound stillness. This was on the nineteenth day of the first month in the eleventh year of the Hongwu era.
His dharma-grandson, Fanyi, carried his remains back; within the bones, *śarīra* relics were clustered like pearls.
On the day of the Buddha’s Bathing Festival, a burial pit was dug beside the ancestral mound, and they were interred there.
Chan Master Zhiren of Wanshou Monastery in Suzhou styled himself as the "Hermit of Tranquility" (Danjuzi) and also as the "Elder of Joyful Serenity" (Xiyisou).
His clan name was Wu, and he was a native of Fanyang. His father, Zhonghua, served as a Professor of Literature at Jiangzhou.

When [Zhiren] was five years old, his father sent him to receive instruction from Master Zhenmu Chun at Ba’en Monastery in the prefecture; at seven, he received full ordination. From childhood, his insight and understanding were transcendent.
Fuying was an extraordinary child from his youth. When he traveled west from his native land to attend an imperial summons by Emperor Yingzong, he stayed at Baoen Temple.
There he met Master [Zhao] Daoyi, who marveled at him and instructed him in the Vinaya. He was then directed to consult with Yuansou. Upon seeing Fuying, Yuansou looked at him and laughed heartily;

Fuying was at a loss for what to do and consequently failed to perform his prostrations on the meditation platform. Yuansou rebuked him, saying, "Go to the hall for practice. One day, Yuansou saw Fuying and asked, "Where are you from?"
The Master said, "Fanyang. The Old Man asked, "How wide is Lake Fanyang? The Master extended his hands in a gesture of measuring it.
The Old Man said, "Not so, not so. The Master replied, "Shut that stinking mouth! He then appointed him to attend to the incense and subsequently took charge of the record-keeping office.
The Old Man once said to the assembly, "Ren, the Record-keeper, has the body of a tiger with the wings of a bird. Later, he appeared in the world at Dechang in Qi and was later transferred to Yue.
At Yunzheng, he honored the state of Wu by performing rites for its longevity. Once, while in his room, the Master held up a wooden pillow and asked a monk, "What is this?
The monk replied, "I know that the Master’s compassionate heart is most earnest. The Master then threw the pillow to the ground.
The monk hesitated to speak. The Master immediately shouted him out. He addressed the assembly: "This illusory body is approaching its end; I shall walk beneath the pines and sleep upon the rocks.
Take care, O dragon and elephant assembly of Beishan! When will the discourse of the Putong era be fulfilled?

Ascending the hall, he said: "Layer upon layer, the distant mountains are green; far away, the river waters are lush. All day long at Xiaowu Pavilion, leaning against the railing, one can never look enough. Suddenly—

He called for his attendant to take up the whisk and then descended from the seat. He ascended the hall and said: "The nature of Chan is birthless; it is free from the conceptualization of Chan as birth.
The nature of Chan is non-abiding; it is free from the stillness of Chan as abiding. On Mount Wutai, clouds steam rice; before the steps of the Buddha Hall, it is a dog’s urine-sky.
At the top of the flagpole, fried noodles are being cooked; three monkeys toss coins at night. At the beginning of the Hongwu era, the Emperor [invited him].
He summoned the Master on account of matters concerning spirits and deities; the Master composed a written response based on the Buddha’s intent, which the Emperor received with great joy.
On the day of Gui-chou, Wei Gong Guan of Puqi became the Governor of Suzhou; seeing the ruins of Wanshou Monastery, he was moved with sorrow and resolved to restore it.
Hearing that the Master was staying at Mount Huqiu, he dispatched an envoy with letters and gifts. After three rounds of travel back and forth, the Master responded.
In his later years, he lived in leisure within a hermitage among the pine forests; his peers did not dare address him by name, all referring to him as "Master Pine Forest.

On the full moon of the third month in the fifteenth year, he manifested illness. On the nineteenth day, his fellow practitioner Ruyong Zhong came to inquire after him, saying, "The Master is departing. All...
"The Master is here by my side. Why not grant me a single word as my final instruction? The Master said, "The Bhagavāns of the ten directions share one and the same path to the gate of Nirvāṇa.
[Zhaozhou] said, "I have been close friends with you for fifty autumns; after this parting, I shall go directly to the Pure Land to meet you.
The Master spoke in a stern voice, "The entire great trichiliocosm is this very Pure Land; where would we not meet? After a long silence, [Zhaozhou] passed away.
He took up his brush and wrote a verse, then passed away in profound stillness. His secular age was seventy-four, and his monastic seniority (śrāmaṇera-avarṣa) was sixty-seven.
Chan Master Mengtang Tanne of Ruilong in Mingzhou was the son of the Wang family of Cixi; both his grandfather and father held prominent official positions.

His mother was Lady Zhou. From childhood, the Master possessed far-reaching aspirations; as he grew older, he became widely versed in the Classics and Histories, and his literary talent blossomed with profound vigor.

At the age of twenty-three, he informed his mother of his intention to leave the household life. He went to follow Xueting at Changlu, whereupon he shaved his head and received the full precepts at Zhaokong.
He studied all the various schools of doctrine and their respective systems without exception. After some time, Xueting moved to reside at Lingyin, and the Master [followed him].
He went again to attend him, serving for over a year until Xueting passed away. Chan Master Jizhao Duan came to fill his position;
upon seeing him, they were in perfect accord, and he immediately appointed him to oversee the internal records (*neiji*).
Later, he appeared in the world at Baosheng in Qingyuan, then moved to Kaishou in Cixi, Guoqing in Tiantai, and finally resided at Ruelong on Mount Xiang. He ascended the hall and held up his whisk.
This very thing, when with Linji, is great capacity and great function, where rolling up and unfolding, seizing and releasing, killing and giving life are all free and at ease.
When with Yunmen, it is solitary and perilous, towering and steep, held up beyond the ordinary, and decided before a word is spoken. When with Caodong, the family style is dense and subtle;
like a golden needle and a jade thread, they meet clearly in the dark. When with Guiyang, there is the father’s kindness and the son’s filiality, and its application—
The matter of the sword’s edge is a trap for tigers; within the Dharma-eye, arrow-points meet, the mind is empty, phenomena are exhausted, emotions are ended, and views are eliminated.
Although the proclamations of the Five Houses possess a resonance like gold and jade that transcends past and present, they are all merely provisional arrangements of the gate.
Not a single direct word has ever been spoken. Tell me, what is this directness?
He cut off a phrase and said in a loud voice, "Look beneath your feet! He ascended the hall and said: "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven;
seven, six, five, four, three, two, one. The Yellow River flows in nine bends from Kunlun. Mahāprajñāpāramitā. The Master would frequently admonish his disciples, saying:
"In studying the school of Emptiness, you must cast aside your physical form and forget both sleep and food, so as to exhaust the karmic burdens accumulated over kalpas."

Only after the purification of past habitual tendencies does the ground of the mind become luminous. From then on, he ate but one meal a day and sat in meditative concentration throughout the night until dawn.
One day, he suddenly prepared for a bath, changed his clothes, and brought out his belongings to distribute as gifts to his friends. He gathered the assembly and spoke this verse:
"I have a thing that has neither back nor face; you must discern it clearly after my parinirvāṇa. Having finished speaking, he sat upright and passed away.
His secular age was eighty-nine. His disciples, including Zhìyán, performed the cremation and enshrined his remains in a stupa at Guoqing Monastery.
Chan Master Fuyuan Fubao of Jingshan, Hangzhou, was a native of Ninghai, Tiantai. His clan name was Fang and his mother’s surname was Zhang.
He left the household life at Chongfu Monastery on Liangzhu in Hangzhou. At that time, Princess Mei of Shihu was the abbess of Jingci Monastery; the Master went there to visit her.
Hu honored him as his teacher and subsequently shaved his head and received full ordination. He went to attend upon Yuansou at Mount Jing. Yuansou asked, "Where have you recently departed from?
The Master replied, "Jingci. Yuansou asked, "What have you come here to do? The Master said, "I have long admired your reputation for the Way and have come specifically to pay my respects.
Yuansou asked, "When Zhaozhou met Nanquan, what did he say? The Master replied, "His head touches the heavens and his feet tread the earth. Yuansou—
The old man asked, "After seeing this, what then? The Master replied, "When hungry, I eat; when weary, I sleep. The old man said, "Where did you learn such empty talk?

The Master replied, "Today I have seen the Master in person. The old man nodded in approval. He subsequently took up residence at Lushan in Cixi, then moved to Dongshan, and later to Mingmen in Siming.
At the beginning of the Hongwu era, he was summoned by imperial decree as a monk of eminent conduct.
The Master went to the capital and was hosted at Tianjie Temple. He entered the inner court several times, and his responses were in accord with the Emperor's wishes.

After staying for three years, he was granted leave to return to Zimen. Later, he presided over Jingshan twice. Entering the hall, he said: "To mention one, you cannot mention two; to let go of one point, you fall into the second.
When the ancients spoke thus, they were truly like those who embrace their stolen goods while crying out for innocence. Dongshan... [text ends]
Not so. To raise two is to fail to raise one; to let one point pass by is to fall into the seventh stage.
At this point, you must further know that there is a path leading upward before you can succeed. What is this path leading upward? After a long silence, he said:

"Do not linger over the green grass on cold crags; sitting amidst white clouds, the essence of the school is not yet perfected. He then ascended the hall and said: "When one leaf falls, the whole world [falls]."
Autumn. A single mote of dust arises; the great earth is gathered up. Who would say that Northern Uttarakuru is not Southern Jambudvīpa?

One has already mounted the ox, yet seeks the ox further. [He] ascends the hall. "Speech is slander; silence is deception. Is there anyone who does not involve themselves in either? He strikes the meditation seat. It is already too late;
he has merely provided a pretext for the ignorant to harbor their conceits. [He] ascends the hall. "One word, one silence; one action, one..."
"Stop! It is like mercury falling to the ground. A monk asked Zhaozhou, "I beg the Master for instruction.
Zhaozhou said, "Have you eaten your congee yet? The monk replied, "I have finished eating. Zhaozhou said, "Go wash your bowl. Ascending the hall, he said:
"All day long I wear clothes, yet never a single thread has hung upon me; all day long I eat rice, yet never a single grain has been chewed. It is like the earth supporting a mountain."
One does not know the mountain’s solitary loftiness until one realizes it is like stone containing jade; one does not know the jade is flawless until one has seen it.
Do not seek the Buddha, do not seek the Dharma, do not seek the Sangha. [The Master] took up his staff and said: "Sometimes riding upon the bright moon, I travel alone across the vast sea.
One day, he fell gravely ill. When his attendant requested a verse, the Master rebuked him, saying: "I still have three years of my worldly life remaining."
The year passed, and it was exactly as he had said. On the day of his passing, he suddenly clapped his hands and said, "A-he-he! O assembly, what is this?

Having finished speaking, he became silent. His secular age was eighty-four, and his years as a monk were sixty-four. His disciples enshrined his entire body and buried it on the right ridge of Jizhao.
Chan Master Liaohan Falin of Lingyin Bamboo Spring in Hangzhou was surnamed Huang. A native of Ninghai in Taizhou, he left the household life under Chan Master Taixu Fayan.
While contemplating the words of Muzhou, he attained awakening and said to Taixu, "From birth until death, it is simply this;
it does not depend on anyone else. He subsequently went to visit Yuansou at Zhongzhu, where Yuansou—
The Master asked, "Where have you come from? The teacher replied, "From Tiantai. The old man asked, "Have you seen Hanshan and Shide?
The teacher joined his palms forward and said, "Today I have personally met the Monk. The old man said, "You liar and deceiver! Go to the hall!

He subsequently had him serve as the incense attendant and then take charge of the storehouse keys. One day, while they were reading the sutras, the old man asked, "Are you reading the sutras? The teacher replied, "Yes."
The old man asked, "With what do you look? The Master replied, "I look with my eyes. The old man held up his fist and said, "Why do you not say, 'Look at this'?
The Master said, "Put down your fist; with what will you look? The old man smiled. When Dongyu took up residence at Jingci, he invited the Master to share the seat [of the abbot].
At that time, Zhuyuan was residing at Fushan; upon hearing the Master’s teachings and proclamations, he praised him without ceasing.

Xunmei composed a verse, which was the foremost among the five hundred members of the assembly. It contained the lines: "Excellently understanding [the truth], one is fit to be a teacher of humans and devas.

The Master resided in the Meng Hall of Jingci Monastery for nine years without stepping outside his door. The Left Chancellor of the Provincial Administration, Duke Tuohan, invited him to preside over Wanshou Monastery, and he subsequently moved to Zhongzhu.
Upon reaching the Buddha Hall, he said: "Dust is brushed away to reveal the Buddha; who knows that the Buddha, too, [is but a construct]?"

This is mere dust. Rarely does one encounter a guest who pierces their own ears; often one sees a person who marks the boat [after the sword has already been lost]. Entering the hall, he said: "The Dharma is the eternal Dharma; the Way is the eternal Way.
To press against and shatter the gateway of the face—when the point is reached, it is not yet arrived. Xuefeng’s assembly of one thousand seven hundred people were spiritual friends.
Morning and evening, he merely rolls three wooden balls. Zhaozhou, a veteran Chan practitioner of seven hundred years, says to everyone he meets, simply, "Go drink tea.
Zhongfeng lives amidst constant sight of this; when brothers visit one another, they do nothing but exchange greetings of seasonal well-being, burn incense, and join their palms.
If you are a true offspring of the golden-maned lion, you will certainly encounter a paradox even three thousand miles away. The fourth year of Zhizhi (1268).
In the year [of his appointment], he moved to Lingyin. Ascending the hall, he cited a monk’s question to Zhaozhou:
“When the myriad dharmas return to the One, where does that One return? Zhaozhou said, “I made a cotton shirt in Qingzhou that weighs seven catties.
The Master said, “Although Zhaozhou skillfully used the Great Sword to cut off this monk’s tongue, he could not avoid airing his own family’s dirty laundry. At Lingyin, it is not so.”
Suddenly, a monk asked, "All phenomena return to the One; where does the One return? He replied to him, "Today is as hot as yesterday.
He ascended the hall and said: "The famous mountain of Lingyin is within the jurisdiction of Old Hangzhou. It was established during the Xianhe era of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Dharma Master Hui-li was its first patriarch. Today is the auspicious festival of Shangyuan, when lanterns are lit in all places. Do you know [why]?"
"Each of you administrators, take care of the wind and the candle. He then descended from his seat and performed the cremation for the late monk, Supervisor Sen.
"The myriad phenomena of the universe are all sealed by the One Dharma. Right now, I have removed the diamond circle and the thorny jujube for you.
What do you call 'the One Dharma'? Two arises from one; do not cling even to the one. A crow in the fire."
Guī let out a lion’s roar; the Great Dragon soared through the void from his seat. Grand Master Xingji sent gifts to invite the Master, but he declined and did not go.
The envoy made three successive trips back and forth, yet the Master remained hidden in the mountains of Kuījī.

The Head of the Monastery (Xíngyuàn), realizing he could not force him, drafted a formal petition requesting that the Master continue to lead Línghǐ. After another three years, he retired to Liàohuàn Ān. This was in the fifteenth year of the Zhìpíng era.

In the spring, he was afflicted with a slight illness. On the second day of the second month, he gathered the assembly to recount the beginning and end of his life’s conduct, and exhorted them, saying:
"The decline of the Buddha-dharma has never been more severe than it is today; you should each exert yourselves. My worldly karmic conditions have come to an end here."
He took up his brush and wrote a verse, saying: "Seventy-two years as a wedge driven into empty space; the final phrase—unspeakable, unspeakable. Thereupon, he passed away peacefully.
His remains stayed in the funerary shrine for ten days without the color of his face changing. He was buried whole at the west of Songyuan Pagoda.
At that time, an ancient cassia tree before the pagoda blossomed in spring; its fragrant scent filled the road, and all who saw it marveled at the wonder.
Scholar Huang Jinqing inscribed his stupa.
Chan Master Guding Zu of Mount Jing in Hangzhou was the son of the Ying family of Yingcheng in Fonghua, Mingzhou. He received his monastic training at Jinye.
When Yuansou resided at Lingyin, the Master went there to pay his respects. One day, during a private interview, he inquired about Huanglong’s encounter with Ciming.

The Old Man asked, "As for Zhaozhou saying, 'The old woman of Mount Tai has been exposed by me,' and Cimeng laughing and saying, 'Is that an insult?'—do you say that the application of these two elders was the same or different? The Master replied, "A pair of unperforated iron hammers.
The Old Man said, "What if Huanglong had attained enlightenment directly beneath them? The Master replied, "That too is a sickness."

He saw empty flowers before his eyes. The old man said, "It is not so, it is not so. As the Master was about to offer a word in response, the old man gave a shout. At that moment, the Master experienced a vast, unobstructed clarity.

The old man appointed him to serve as the head of the secretarial office (*jishi*). The Master became even more humble and self-effacing. At the age of fifty-four, he first entered the world to preside over Longjiao Temple, followed by Baota, and then Zhongtianzhu.
In the seventh year of the Zhi Zheng era, he moved to Jingshan. The Emperor of the Yuan dynasty conferred upon him the title "Hui... [The text ends here].
Chan Master Xingwen Minhong Juepuji. A monk asked, "Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different?
The Master said, "A broken winnowing basket gives birth to a broom. The monk bowed and said, "Thank you for the instruction, Master.
The Master said, "Last night at the third watch, I lost my ox; when dawn came, I had lost my fire. [The monk] asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "A weight."
Dipping [the chopsticks] in vinegar. [The monk] asked, "What is the matter that lies beyond? The Master said, "Looking up, one does not see the sky.
[The monk] said, "I remember a monk asking Yunmen, 'What is the Buddha? and Yunmen replied, 'A dried-up shit-stick. What about that?
The Master said, "Yunmen was not being kind-hearted. The monk said, "How far apart are a dried-up shit-stick and dipping [chopsticks] in vinegar? The Master said:
"In the boiling cauldron, there is no place for cold. As the monk prepared to offer a word in response, the Master gave a shout. Ascending the hall, he said:

"I shall place the worlds of the ten directions upon the eyelashes of all of you, without the slightest movement. I shall pour the waters of the four great oceans beneath the heels of all of you, without a single drop flowing away.
One who understands medicine has few ailments; one who knows their lot has little sorrow. Ascending the hall, he raised the example of Da... [text fragment]

Master Guyizhi addressed the assembly, saying: "We are all gathered here to eat some radish soup. If you call it 'a stalk of radish soup,' you will enter hell as fast as a shot arrow. The Master said:
"A patriarch’s way of dealing with people is like that of a household infected by *gudu* (poisonous fungi).

They place poison within their food and drink and give it to others; they never fail to wish to sever the person's life-root (*mūla*). Even so, there are those who become karmic enemies through this."

"How many people are there who can truly do so? Whenever Minister Keng-li visited the Master to inquire about the profound principles of the Chan school, on one occasion, while the Master was reading a scripture, the Minister asked him, "Why are you not reading the scriptures?
The Master replied, "Is merely following the lines and counting the characters what constitutes reading the scriptures? The Minister was speechless.
The Master turned over the pages of the scripture and said, "I am off to read the scriptures. The Minister covered the scripture with his hand and said, "I request that the Master [continue to]..."

He spoke thus: "The Master said, 'Who were Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou? In the year of Jǐxū (1358), as he was about to pass into *nirvāṇa*, he wrote a letter entrusting his protection to the Chancellor.
He further composed a verse, saying: 'Birth and death are pure and true; the great void is perfectly full.
At seventy-nine years, the cradle rope has snapped. Having cast down his brush, he passed away. During the cremation, his tongue and his prayer beads remained unburnt. [The text ends here.]
His benefits were incalculable. At Mount Jing, Longjiao, and Putuo, he was interred in separate pagodas. His secular age was seventy-nine and his monastic seniority fifty-five.
His recorded sayings from four assemblies, along with an external collection, circulate in the world.
Chan Master Gu’an Zhongyou Zuchan of Tianning Monastery in Mingzhou was of the Chen clan and a native of Ningbo. He received the tonsure and full ordination under Chan Master Kuang of Fozhi.

Having studied under Jizhao at Mount Jing, he attained the essential meaning [of the Dharma]. He emerged from seclusion at Lushan, subsequently moved to Xiangshan, and was later promoted to Tianning Monastery in the prefecture.
Upon ascending the hall, he said: "If one speaks of the First Phrase, the Buddhas of the three periods cannot speak it."
The six generations of patriarchs could not speak it; the old monks of the world could not speak it;
this mountain monk cannot speak it; the great assembly cannot speak it. [The Master] picks up his staff: Can this staff speak it?
Even if it could, that would still be the second phrase. [He] ascends the hall: "This very mind is Buddha; neither mind nor Buddha; not mind, not Buddha. Wutai Mountain.
Clouds above steam rice; before the steps of the Buddha Hall, the sky is as clear as dog urine; atop the pinnacle of the *kṣa* pole, a frying pan is being heated;
three monkeys toss coins at night. On the occasion of the Lantern Festival, he ascends the hall: "Before the fifteenth day, head and tail are golden lotuses;
after the fifteenth day, white oxen and tabby cats run in packs. On this very fifteenth day, the pavilions..."
The fire above and the fire below illuminate one another; the carriages and horses pass back and forth as people watch people. Good assembly! But tell me, in what way is it good?
It is difficult to deceive the eyes of the multitude. [He] then descended from his seat.
Chan Master Yuzhong Shanru of Kaiyuan Temple in Suzhou was a native of Wujiang. He ascended the hall and said:
"The Buddha-body pervades the entire Dharma-realm and appears universally before all sentient beings.

Why was it that when the residents of Hudu and followers of Huang-Lao welcomed him, the wind and waves became so terrifying that the image immediately sank? Yet when Zhu Ying of Wu County and the nun Dongling Bo invited it..."
The numinous forms were majestic as they floated side by side; when [the monk] attempted to lift them up, they suddenly ascended the boat.

The two stone images of Vaiśravaṇa and Kāśyapa currently enshrined in the mountain are these very ones. Is this not the case that, while responding to conditions and reaching all beings without exception, they have always remained upon this Bodhi seat?
Even so, if you understand it in such a way, you are like a tiger watching a water mill.
Do not understand it in such a way; look from Zhenzhou toward Changlu. Cast away both "such" and "not such. And how about this?
In a world of peace and clarity, there is no need for deceptive words. The Master’s words are never uttered in vain. When requested for verses, he would write them down as they came to him.
He composed a verse for a monk at Cao’an, saying: The National Teacher is a virtuous friend for ten thousand generations. At the Grass Hut on Mount Yandang.

When the world hears that one has obtained residence therein, they conceive the thought that such an encounter is difficult to find and strive to repay this profound kindness. A certificate of ordination descends directly from heaven;

having obtained it, how could its value be worth less than ten thousand pieces of gold? If one does not cultivate the monastic practice during this time, one will bring shame upon the sincere heart of the Emperor and the King.
In his later years, the Master, for the sake of the Dharma, resided at Wanshou Monastery with his dharma-son Huáng Yíngzhōng and expanded [the monastery].
Yan invited him to his residence to care for his aged parents. When Xiang Benkong succeeded him on the seat, he treated him with even greater courtesy;
thus, [Xuanjue] was able to dwell at ease, delighting in the Way. He once resided at Zhizhi Monastery by Fengmen, and people consequently called him Master Zhizhi.
As he was about to pass away, he called his sons to bid them farewell; then, with serene composure, he departed this life.
Myan Benwu, a Dharma Master of Shangzhu Monastery in Hangzhou, was a native of Huangyan. He received the tonsure under Fangshan at Jingci Monastery.
Jizhao held the reins of leadership at Zhongzhu. His maternal uncle, a venerable elder of the monastic academy, urged him to change his sectarian affiliation.
Thereupon, he visited Zhandang at Yanfu Temple and devoted himself to the study of the doctrinal schools. Jizhao regretted his departure and sent him a verse, saying:

"Entering Chan through the Teachings has occurred in both ancient and modern times; Entering the Teachings through Chan has never existed from antiquity to the present. The single mind and the three contemplations..."

"Though the gates are distinct, the moon remains solitary as it fills the waters of a thousand rivers. Later, having entered the world as a successor to Zantang, he nevertheless burned a single incense stick to honor Jizhao;
he did not allow their differing traces to create a duality in his mind. When Jizhao passed away, the Master was residing at Yanqing in Siming.
He sent a letter entrusting him with the vigorous propagation of the essential tenets of the teachings, saying nothing else. Regarding this, the Master...
At the sacrificial banquet, he offered incense, saying: "The fifth transmission of Wuxi is most radiant; Jizhao’s single generation is a gate of ambrosia.
To casually touch it is to have one's liver and brain split open; Ice and frost suddenly become the warmth of spring. I think back to the day my nostrils were struck away."
What breath remains now? The celestial wind blows from the north as the year draws to a close.
Like a flash of lightning seeking a trace in the void, he passed away seated without illness.
Chan Master Chuzhen of Wanshou Monastery in Suzhou sent this verse to Attendant Zhong:
"When Niaoke blew up his cloth hair, the attendant attained enlightenment on the spot. This pair of unperforated iron hammers is nothing but the display of a ghost’s livelihood."

If one is a sharp and discerning master, possessing a natural and innate air of magnanimity, they will expand the radiant light of the original ground and manifest the very core of the monk’s realization.
They will encompass the great thousandfold world-system within the tip of a single hair and contain Mount Sumeru within a mustard seed;
they walk directly upon the crown of Vairocana’s head, and even the Great Compassionate One with a thousand hands cannot restrain them.
Chan Master Wufang Zhipu of Ba’en was a dharma successor of Chan Master Wan of Jiangxin. He was a native of Guiyang, of the Long clan. While residing at the monastery, he ascended the hall and said:
"In the sixth month, a traveler’s mouth spews smoke; all this toil is but for the sake of profit and fame. How can one compare such a person to the disinterested guest beneath the forest trees?"
Jue woke up with his robe at dawn and slept again. He struck the meditation seat and said, "Ganming, do not spare your verbal karma; I shall explain it through for you.
On the thirtieth day of the twelfth lunar month, Old Yan will demand from you the payment for your meals. He ascended the hall and said: "The spring colors are thick; the spring days are bright.
The gardens and groves are warm; the wild peach blossoms are red. In the past, Lingyun saw through them upon one glimpse and was liberated from form and emptiness. Now..."
Everyone sees it all together; why then do they not awaken? If they do not awaken, their eyes are caged by forms. (He strikes the whisk.
To mistakenly teach people is to resent the wind at the fifth watch.
The Great Chan Master Xiaoyin of Yunju in Nankang Prefecture once presented this verse to the Chan practitioner Xin:
"Faith is the source of the Way and the mother of merit; If medicine proves effective, it does not require much. If you, O noble one, can directly accept and take it up,"
How could even the Buddhas and Patriarchs do anything against him?

Shuili Yuan-shan Ran was exceptionally brilliant from his youth. Initially, he went to see Yishan Wan; subsequently, he was sent to Baizhang to study under Huiji.
Upon seeing him, Huiji held him in high esteem and appointed him as head of the secretariat. One day, he asked:

"Huanglong had already attained the essential meaning at Letan and led his disciples on a journey to travel and seek teachers. Yet, when he met Ciming, his spirit was drained and he broke into a cold sweat. Where did his error lie?"

As the Master was about to answer, the [other] practitioner suddenly let out a thunderous shout. At that moment, the Master’s doubts were completely dispelled like ice melting away.

Later, because his fellow practitioners pressed him with difficult questions, the Master replied with this verse: "Bai Zhang’s wild fox, the wild fox of Bai Zhang, Buried together in a single pit— May you rest in peace.

He was granted the title "Great Chan Master Guangzhi Quanwu" (Extensive Wisdom and Complete Enlightenment). Furthermore, he was summoned by imperial decree to the capital, where he had an audience with the Emperor at the Quanzhang Pavilion;

He stepped down from the hall and entered the new temple to ascend the seat. The primary truth (paramārtha-satya) is as bright as the shining sun and as vast as the great void;
the myriad phenomena stand in dense array, yet not a speck of dust is established. To cite the present or invoke the past is nothing but to produce branches outside the joints.

He gathers the ocean of three thousand worlds within a single seal and fully encompasses eighty thousand dharma-gates upon a single hair-tip.

Just as the Bodhisattvas at the assembly of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra attained the liberation door of the inexhaustible treasury of merit, he produces various delicious foods and drinks from a single vessel;

The drums resounded spontaneously; the chanting of the *brahman* hymns and songs was naturally performed.

When he picks them up, they are pierced through in every direction; every single point manifests the boundless wondrous body. When he sets them down, they mirror the earth and illuminate the heavens;

"How is my hand like a Buddha’s hand? How is my foot like a donkey’s foot? Every person has their own 'birth-condition' (shengyuan); which one is the birth-condition of this venerable monk? The Master said:

In the fifth month of the fourth year of the Zhizheng era (1344), he manifested a slight illness and wrote a letter of parting to bid farewell to his disciples.
While traveling, he instructed his disciples to use the gold and silk bestowed by two successive reigns to construct a Ten-Thousand-Buddha Pavilion as an offering to repay the national grace.

On the twenty-second day, he wrote a verse, sat in the lotus position, and passed away. On the sixteenth day of the eighth month of autumn that year, he was buried on the rear ridge of the pagoda courtyard at Shitou City.
He was sixty-one years of age and forty-six years since his ordination. [This record is by] Huang Wenxian Gong.

Wenming composed his epitaph, and the collected works of Duke Yu Wenjing recorded his life’s achievements. In the *jiayin* year of the Hongwu era, he was reinterred at Boyun Mountain, adjacent to the ancient stupa of the monk Kang Senghui.

His writings include the *Chanyuan Qinggui* (Pure Rules for Chan Monasteries) and the *Sihui Yulu* (Recorded Sayings of the Four Assemblies), as well as the *Pushi Ji* (Pufang Collection), all of which have been circulated in the world.
Chan Master Nianchang of Meiwu in Xiangfu, Jiaxing Prefecture, was surnamed Huang and was a native of Huating. His father was Wenyou and his mother was Lady Yang.
Having prayed for an heir before an image of Avalokiteśvara (Dabei), one night she dreamed of an elderly monk seeking lodging; consequently, she became pregnant.
On the twelfth day of the third month in the Renwu year of the Zhizhi era (1262), he was born. That night, divine light illuminated the room and a wondrous fragrance pervaded the air.
The Master delighted in sitting alone from his youth. At the age of twelve, he entered the monastic order under Tizhi at Yuanming Monastery in Pingjiang.
At fourteen, he shaved his head and received full ordination. In the year Wushen of the Zhida era, Fozhi Huiji moved from Baiyang in Jiangxi to Jingci in Hangzhou;
the Master went there to attend upon him. He happened to encounter Fozhi ascending the hall and citing the story of Upāsaka Fu of Taiyuan hearing the sound of a horn.
A Verse on the Circumstances of Awakening the Way says: Qinsheng entered the vast ocean; Taishi traveled to famous mountains.

From this point onward, along the road outside the city of Yangzhou, strict orders were issued that the gates were not to be opened early. The Master attained sudden enlightenment upon hearing these words.

He went to the master’s quarters and presented his understanding. Fozhi nodded in approval and appointed him to oversee the record office. When Fozhi later moved to Mount Jing, the Master succeeded him in that position.
He served as the head of the assembly. In the year Bingchen, by imperial selection, he ascended to the abbacy of Xiangfu.
His works include the twenty-two fascicles of the *Fozu Tongzai*.
Chan Master Shishu Zuying of Xuedou in Mingzhou was the son of the Chen family of Wujiang.
Having entered the monastic life at the Puxiang Temple as a young boy, he received the full precepts by shaving his head at the age of fifteen and immediately set out on foot to travel for study.
Initially, he followed Xugu Ling at Mount Yang; hearing of the renown of Huiji at Mount Jing, he went there to seek him out. Upon their first meeting, they reached a state of mutual accord.
He remained as the *zhǔjì* (chief administrator). Later, he emerged into the world and presided over Mingzhi Lóngjiào, then moved to Wànshòu in Hángzhōu, and subsequently to Xuědòu and Yùwáng.
There is a verse by Xiè Tiāntóng Píngshí Dǐ inquiring after his illness, which says: "This body is without self, yet the roots of illness run deep.
I am ashamed that Mañjuśrī has come so far to visit me. There are naturally mountain flowers to discuss non-duality; Facing each other before the green lamp, we laugh and chant."
The Dharma-body pervades all places; eating rice or eating emptiness, one attains freedom. At Taibai on Mount Mao, amidst mist and rain, the bamboo shoots coming and going are also elegant.
In his later years, he suffered from paralysis; he constructed a small shrine and called it "Wooden Robes."

He sat within it daily, never engaging in worldly affairs. In the third month of the *guīwèi* year of the Zhèngtóng era (1363), he saw a woman in tattered clothing who prostrated herself and requested that the Master take rebirth as a king.
The Master replied, "I have no desire to be born into the family of a celestial king. Seventeen days later, he passed away while sitting in the lotus posture.
His verse at the moment of death read: "For fifty-three years I played with cleverness until I became clumsy; I have trampled through..."
The void walks barefoot; the myriad phenomena and the celestial host laugh without ceasing.
Chan Master Zhongzhu Yiguan Zhengqiu was a native of Fanyang. His clan name was Fang. He went to study under Huiji at Jingci Monastery.
Huiji asked, "Where are you from? The Master replied, "Fanyang. Huiji asked, "How deep is the water in the lake of Fanyang?"
The Master said, "Staring with wide-open eyes, one does not see the bottom. Jiji said, "If that is so, then even the nostrils of a patch-robed monk will be soaked and rotted away.
The Master said, "I certainly do not borrow the nostrils of the Abbot to breathe. Jiji said, "In the end, whose nostrils do you borrow to breathe?"
The Master said, "I respectfully wish the Abbot ten thousand blessings. Ji-ken appointed him as attendant (*śaikṣa*). After more than two years had passed, he went to Mount Tianmu to visit Zhongfeng.

He then visited Jingshan to see Yuansou, who charged him with the duties of the Record Keeper (*karmadāna*). When Xiaoyin presided over Zhongzhu Monastery, he had the Master share the teaching seat (*pīṭha*).

He subsequently took up residence at Chongyin in Jinling, where the Imperial Preceptor conferred upon him the title "Buddha-Sun Universal Illumination" (*Buddhāditya-samantaprabha*). He was later transferred to Feng...

Shan Zifu was promoted to serve the state at the Main Temple (Zhujibao). He was subsequently transferred to Zhongzhu, where he addressed the assembly, saying: "The mind is not the Buddha; wisdom is not the Way.
A single thought involving deliberation causes the whole body to enter the weeds. Therefore it is said: 'Before one's eyes there is no dharma,' yet the intent lies before one's eyes.
It is not a dharma of the present moment; it is beyond what the ears and eyes can reach. Throughout all time, heaven and earth..."
The sun and moon; the mountains and rivers of past and present; the human relations of past and present—each and every thing is manifest, each and every object is fully revealed.
It is not borrowed from the thousand sages; it is not sought through the myriad functions. Within and without, there is nothing to take up; throughout past and present, there is no location.
To understand it in such a way is still to mistake a donkey’s saddle for one’s father’s chin. Nevertheless, since this is Sizhou...

His worldly age was fifty-seven and his monastic seniority was forty-four.
Chan Master Zhongfang Tiantun of Foyan in Mingzhou was the son of the Zhang family of Xiangshan. From his youth, he was precocious and intelligent.

He went to Tianning Monastery in Guangde to receive the tonsure under Master Zhuyuan. Zhuyuan said, "Your aspirations are vast and far-reaching; you are fit to uphold the Great Dharma. Do not let me hold you back.
Thereupon, he went to see Yong of Dongzhou at Huqiu Monastery. Once, while passing through the Sandalwood Grove, he viewed the *Biographies of Eminent Monks* together with a monk.

When the Three Sages meet people, they speak. The Master said: "Those two great elders stole a mere fragment of Linji’s private property and each went about showing it off.
If one were to examine them closely, it would be better to bury them all together in a single pit. When a fellow student arrived, he ascended the hall.
The scenery was cool and crisp; companions visited in solitude. Brewing tea by the mountain stream, burning firewood in the mountain caves—this is the compassion [of the Buddhas].
The Patriarch used the property of the monastery as his own personal gift. Tianyi was not like this:

he offered flowers to the Buddha without fuss and brewed no tea for his guests. Do not disdain his lack of formal etiquette; such simplicity is the way of the monk. (When the Master appeared in the world at Tianyi, he was already eighty-six years old.

There was a preface by Master Le Qitan which said: "When the great Peng raises its wings, it soars high; when the peach of immortality blooms, how could it be late? It further said: "It is fitting that the Elder of Tuṣita descended to pay homage, just as King Zhou of Xi obtained Lü Yang and brought him back with him.")
He did not seek fame at the expense of integrity; he was also a peer of the venerable Master Dingyin.
Chan Master Yixi Zirú of Zhongzhú in Hangzhou was a successor of Chan Master Jingshan. He was a native of Fújiàn. When the Yuan troops descended upon the South River, the Master was still young.
He was encountered by some traveling soldiers who took him to Lin’an and abandoned him there. A wealthy man of the Hu family took him in and had him accompany his own son to study.

The master stood at the corner of the courtyard and silently memorized everything without missing anything. When the boy grew up, the Hu family had the master enter the local Wuxiang Temple as a monk.
He studied under Yunfeng at Mount Jing and attained the essential instruction. He first resided at Wanshou Monastery. Tian...
In the first month of the calendar year, Xiaoyin Yan of Central India received an imperial decree to open the mountain monastery at Longxiang.

When three candidates were proposed to succeed him as abbot, the Emperor personally marked the Master’s name with his brush. The Xuanzheng Yuan then prepared a formal petition requesting the Master to reside there.

A member of the Huang family, who deeply revered the Master’s spiritual conduct, frequently provided him with *īśvaraprasāda* (vegetarian) offerings. One day, she invited him to her home, where she continued to present these offerings with even greater devotion.
He then opened his private treasury and displayed the gold and jade he stored there to the Master. The Master returned in a state of indignation and said to his disciples:
"That Huang family showed me the treasures from their treasury, intending to entice me to die and become their son.
For one who has left the household life, gold and jade should be regarded as mere rubble. Since ancient times, many have fallen into this trap—not only for the sake of becoming someone's son."
There were those who acted as his cowherds and horsemen; consequently, he severed ties with the Huang family. Later, when he passed away and was cremated, many miraculous signs occurred.
Chan Master Gu Zhizhe of Donglin in Jiangzhou was a native of Duchang. His clan name was Chao. Initially, he resided at Xingguo.
The Venerable Master moved to Donglin. He ascended the hall and said: "The Buddhas of the past have already spoken; the Buddhas of the future shall speak; the Buddhas of the present are speaking now.
But tell me, ultimately what do they speak of? He struck his staff and descended from the seat. He ascended the hall again and said: "When light comes, darkness departs;
when wisdom arises, delusion perishes. A black ox lies dead in stagnant water; a mangy horse is tied to a withered post. How does this compare to [the state of] Dong..."

The village Black King sleeps with his legs outstretched at the yellowing dusk; one sleep lasts until the light of day. When I, this mountain monk, speak thus, you must take care not to misunderstand. Ascending the hall:
The entire command is held up in its essential framework, unfathomable to either sage or commoner. Letting go the guiding thread, I invite all fellow practitioners to join me.
A fragrant breeze blows from the south, and a subtle coolness arises within the halls and pavilions. Ascending the hall: O virtuous Chan practitioners, the Patriarch said:
Perfectly identical to the great void, without lack and without excess. Beneath three rafters and before a single mat seven feet square—strictly avoid relying on others for understanding.
Is there anyone who does not stick their head out through the heavens? Then he said: "Circumambulate the hall to drink tea. He offered a verse at the stupa of Dharma Master Xian:
"The skull has always possessed its own numinous light; How could Xuedou ever have shaken out his entrails? He cut it off.
The grandmother’s three-inch tongue remains to this day as two swords leaning tall against the heavens. A verse for sending Chan person Wan to visit Master Xugu of Mount Jing:
"Ten thousand tracks and a thousand paths are all on one carriage; The eye of one who travels for instruction is correct and never errs.
Among the seventeen hundred [monks], he is the master; Originally, he was the Little Śākyamuni of Mount Yang."
The *Pǔshuō* (General Discourse) of Chan Master Guàishí Qí of Tiāntóng in Míngzhōu states in brief: "Studying Chan is fundamentally neither difficult nor easy;
it requires only that one possess great roots of faith and a resolute will.

Ceasing all myriad activities, not carrying even a single saint, cutting off all conditions, and not retaining a single dharma—like the vast void where no trace remains, like Mount Sumeru standing firm and immovable."
Only when one is immovable can one hope for the unsurpassed True Vehicle. It is further said: "This matter is like being hungry or thirsty;
merely speaking of drink or food cannot provide relief. One must personally drink the water and personally eat the rice to achieve actual efficacy.
It is further said: "In citing the essential instructions of the former sages of old, which were spoken with such poignant urgency for the sake of others, if one can [directly encounter them]..."
In this state, leave the mind empty; do not adhere to the characteristics of dharmas, yet do not depart from them.
To hear this once and awaken immediately—this is precisely the moment when the broad-faced butcher at the Nirvāṇa Assembly cast down his butcher’s blade and became a Buddha on the spot.
It is so, yet you must not understand it in such a way. Excessive words distance one further from the Way. For now, cut through the entanglements! (He lets out a shout.)
Record of Chan Master Benyuan Shanda of Mount Jing in Hangzhou. A native of the Chai family of Xianju, he was a junior seat-holder.
In his youth, he traveled with Jiwang Xin, vowing never to hold formal administrative office. He first met Xueyan at Yangshan; subsequently, he returned to Zhejiang to study under [Master] Jing.
When Shanyunfeng received him into his inner circle, he attained a realization, and Feng certified his attainment. It happened that Huiyun’s seat was vacant, and the Master was appointed to fill it.
Later, he moved to Baoning, Jingci, and Jingshan, where he achieved meritorious records in each. The Master habitually did not set up a bed;
at night, he would burn incense and light candles, sitting upright until dawn, making this his constant practice. Furthermore, his physical constitution was such that...
People differ in their circumstances. When encountering severe cold, he would wear fine linen; when it was intensely hot, he would wear silk or cotton wool.

He once used his alms bowl as the foundation to establish Dayuan Monastery on a mountain halfway along the eastern road to receive visiting monks from all quarters. One day, knowing that the time had come, he gathered the assembly and finished recounting the events of his lifelong travels.
After a short while, he sat upright and passed away in stillness.
The Chief Seat Dragon Rock Jin was repeatedly invited by various quarters, yet he remained lying high in bed and refused to rise. He once composed the "Song of Delighting in Leisure," which says:
"The very mind is Buddha; no-mind is the Way. In all matters, simply follow conditions; I find my own body and mind well.
I have never sought to dwell in a monastery; Even to be a Buddha, I would not do so. I have never upheld the Vinaya, Nor have I ever observed the precepts."
To break through [delusion], letting go or holding fast depends entirely on the person. To cling to the Dharma while practicing is like a donkey pulling a millstone.
If you wish to walk, then walk; if you wish to sit, then sit. Neither diligent nor indolent, take this single scroll of the *Three Character Classic* as your daily task.
At times you walk deep within the bottom of the sea; at times you lie atop the summit of a high mountain. How many lifetimes must one cultivate before achieving this?
Idle people, who would willingly allow themselves to be shackled by empty fame? I do not hold you in contempt; let them spit in my face. How much time can one obtain in a hundred years?
Why must one insist on distinguishing between self and others? Be poor and have no need for worry; be rich and cease being arrogant.
King Yama sends his invitation to all, without partiality toward friend or foe; everyone is delivered unto a single mass of blazing fire. Do it yourself.

Having attained mastery, I shall never let the wind overturn my rudder. To mend what is torn and ward off the cold, I warm myself and then cease; with plain rice and coarse tea, I pass my days as circumstances allow.
I compose songs of joy and leisure, singing them myself and harmonizing with my own voice. It is not that I am a man of leisure who refuses to work; rather, I simply do not wish to be idle.
How many leisurely men are there in this world?

There was the monk Mingzhou Gong, a dharma heir of Chan Master Heshan Ming, who maintained himself with integrity and purity. He recited the Lotus Sūtra daily; it happened that he heard Tiejing ascend the hall.
He eventually attained the essential point of the teaching. Once, while sitting in meditation at night, he composed a verse that said: "A single lamp of oil is exhausted in the mountain window;

The hearth-fire is out, and all is cold and silent. I shall leave the *huatou* for tomorrow’s recitation; The practitioner strikes the bell and ascends the tower again. Because of this, Tiejing praised him upon ascending the hall.
At the time of his death, he passed away peacefully without illness, having changed his robes and sat upright. During the cremation, his tongue remained intact.
Not destroyed.
Chan Master Zhutian Rulin of Xuedou, Mingzhou, successor to the Celestial Youth Chan Master Jue, was a native of the Wang family of Changguo. He followed Master Meijian Fu.
Having shaved his head and received full ordination, he heard of the spiritual transformation of Zhonghong at Tiantong and went there to study under him. Hong appointed him as his attendant.
One day, while in the meditation hall, Hong raised the koan of Zhaozhou’s “The dog has no Buddha-nature,” and the Master attained a sudden and thorough realization.
Subsequently, he met Yuetang Yin at Lingyin; Yin esteemed him and appointed him to oversee the office of the Secretary (Jishi). It happened that his preceptor, Zu Fangyan Hui, was there.
The Chan Master traveled to Shanglan in Longxing, where the Master attended him. While visiting Baiyang, they paid their respects to Huiji, who subsequently appointed him to share the teaching seat.

He later took charge of Xuedou in Mingzhou; in his final years, he presided over Wanshou for barely a year. Suffering from a slight illness, he changed his robes, wrote a verse of farewell, and passed away.
This was on the twenty-fifth day of the fifth month in the fifth year of the Zhizhi era. His body was cremated, and *śarīra* were obtained.
Those with five-colored [halos] as large as beans or grains were beyond counting. His lifespan was sixty-six years and fifty *lǎ* (years of ordination).
Chan Master Simin of Dayu Peak at Daochang Monastery in Huzhou was the son of the Zhang family of Xiangshan.
He first studied under Yunfeng at Mount Jing, and subsequently visited Zhihong at Tiantong. Zhihong asked, "Where have you come from recently? The Master replied, "Mount Jing. Zhihong...
Yunmen said, "How do you speak a single phrase that has not left Mount Jing? The Master replied, "Level as a mirror’s surface, yet as treacherous as a precipice.
Yunmen asked, "Why did the tiger bite the tiger last night before the mountain? The Master was about to offer a word when Yunmen struck him. The Master suddenly attained realization.
One day, while attending him, Yunmen raised the case of the World-Honored One being asked by a non-Buddhist: "I do not ask about existence..."

When [Zhaozhou] said, "I do not ask; there is no word," the World-Honored One remained silent for a long while. "What was the meaning? the Master asked. The Master joined his palms and stepped forward.
Yunhuang said, "The non-Buddhist praised him, saying: 'The World-Honored One is greatly compassionate; he has opened the clouds of my delusion and allowed me to enter. What about that?
The Master replied, "A gentleman loves wealth, but takes it by the right way. Yunhuang, delighted that this matched his own view, ordered him to take charge of the storehouse. Great!
In the fourth year of the Dede era, he emerged from seclusion at Jixiang in Jun. He subsequently moved to Jinwen, Damei, and Baofu.

The Imperial Preceptor bestowed upon him the title "Buddha-Mind Mingmiao" (Wondrously Profound Buddha-Mind). In the third year of the Zhishun era, the Guangjiao Prefecture invited him to preside over Shuanglin.

In the second year of the Yuantong era, the Provincial Administration selected him to reside at Daochang. Addressing the assembly, he said: "This matter is like an iron wall or a silver mountain; it is like a great mass of fire. When they approach...
"You cannot stay; you cannot avoid it. What will you all do? Even if your feet do not touch the ground and you find another path to the heavens, you are still nothing but a damp, useless bucket.
Entering the hall, he said: "To interpret the meaning according to the scriptures is to be at odds with the Buddhas of the three ages.
To depart from even a single word of the scriptures is to speak like a demon. He took up his staff, struck it once, and said: "In the sixth month, it is not hot. Five...
His grains did not ripen. In the fourth month of the third year of the Yuanzhen era, he manifested a slight illness; on the twenty-eighth day, he wrote a verse and passed away.
He was a Dharma successor of Chan Master Yin of Lingyin.
Chan Master Yuejiang Zongjing of Mount Jing in Hangzhou was the son of the Ni family of Jinhua. From childhood, his intelligence was peerless.

At the age of seventeen, he received the precepts from Master Wenyi of Zhengjue Monastery. While reciting the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, he came across the passage: "It is as if a person points with their finger at the moon;
that person, by means of the finger, ought to see the moon. He attained sudden enlightenment. Thereupon, he went to visit Master Yuetang to inquire about the Yellow [River].
When Huangbo struck Linji, how did you understand it? The Master replied, "It is like pressing down an ox's head while it grazes on grass.
Xuedou Qian admired this and appointed him to the position of *weina*. Later, he emerged into the world at Jingshan, where his profound influence spread far and wide.

In his later years, he retired to the East Hall and addressed the assembly, saying: "I have sat firmly blocking Lingxiao for ten years; in upholding the school and discussing the Way, I have merely followed conditions. Now, I shall simply rest."

"Rest!啸月吟风乐自然 (Xiaoyue yinfeng le ziran—Sighing at the moon and chanting with the wind, one delights in spontaneity). On the third day of the tenth month of the Renxu year of the Yuantong era, he manifested a slight illness.
At noon, he gathered the assembly and spoke this verse: "A guest at the gate of the Patriarchs speaks of non-arising;

I, old and worn, understand nothing at all—midday strikes the third watch. Having finished speaking, he sat upright and passed away. He was sixty-seven years of age. His entire body was enshrined in a pagoda.

At Yuanzhao Hermitage, there was Chan Master Wuwai Zongkuo of Donglin in Jiangzhou; he was a native of Nanchang, surnamed Wei. Having long relied upon Yuetang, one day, while in the meditation hall, the Master raised the karmic occasion concerning the saying, "The sound of the stream is entirely the broad and long tongue.
Their spiritual faculties were in accord, and he was subsequently granted the seal of transmission. [Recorded by] Chuchi.
He lived at Shiyunju for some time and later moved to Donglin. When seeing off a monk traveling to Eastern Wu, he composed a verse: "The Buddha was an old bhikṣu from Western Heaven;
For what reason does he lie prostrate in Suzhou? Relying on you, go now and lift him up gently; Ask him about the 'head-word' of two thousand years.
At the time of his death, he gathered the assembly and spoke this verse: "I am seventy-one years old; my worldly ties are now finished. I push..."
He overturned five Mount Sumerus, and at midnight the sun rose; having finished speaking, he passed away.

At Zhongzhu, there was a Chan Master who was the Dharma heir of Chan Master Zhenjue Yuanweng Xin of Shimen in Jiaxing Prefecture. When Zhenjue Kaimeng ascended the hall, he spoke on the "Upward" [teaching].
A single mechanism. The final secret instruction. Not transmitted by Buddhas or Patriarchs; where even the thousand sages are rendered speechless.
Is there anyone who can turn their body and breathe out? Come forth and deliver a message. A monk asked: "The opening of the mountain with a pickaxe has existed since antiquity;
you, Master, now newly open the Stone Gate Barrier. As I pass by on this borrowed path, may I ask one question? The Master said: "Bring your official warrant quickly."
The monk asked, "What is the master of Guanzhong? The Master said, "The Mohe sword lies crosswise in my hand;
I am not yet willing to strike down the dull-witted. The monk hesitated. The Master gave a shout. The monk bowed. The Master said, "You dull-witted fellow! Then he said:
"Rivers and mountains fill the eyes, utterly free from a speck of dust; boundless oceans of lands surround one another. The pavilions of Vairocana appear layer upon layer—who beholds the gate?"
At the gate stands Sudhana. He plants his staff upright; the stone gate is opened, and the true field of awakening is revealed.
Let those coming from the south or the north enter as they please. Small Assembly Sermon: To raise the Dharma banner and establish the fundamental tenet—this is clearly the Buddha’s mandate at Caoxi.

“Great assembly, while raising the Dharma banner is indeed a certainty, what is it to establish the fundamental tenet? Is it not the three turns and five turns, or the raising of the fist? [He strikes down.]
"Hma! Is it silence, sitting firmly in one's seat, and then sweeping away one’s sleeves and departing? Is it the use of words and writing to discuss antiquity and the present?
Is it a dusty head and a soiled face, sitting for long periods without lying down? You must examine this with great care.
If your true eye is not clear, you will fall entirely into partiality, error, and attachment. Therefore it is said: "The supreme flavor of *amṛta* (clarified butter) is for the world..."
What is cherished becomes a poisonous drug when encountered by such people as these. According to my ancestral masters, the entire ten directions of the world are a seamless iron wall;
Bodhidharma did not recognize this. The entire ten directions of the world are a holeless iron hammer; Kāśyapa did not know this.
There is no place for you to deliberate, and no place for you to take up; it turns heaven and revolves earth.

Shifting the constellations and displacing the stars; releasing both and gathering both, penetrating the summit and reaching the bottom. Do you understand? When the dragon’s sleeve is swept aside, the whole body is revealed;
where the Elephant King walks, there is no trace of the fox.
The mother of the layman Lü Tiéchuán, Lady Qin, was born from a dream in which the Abbot of Gōng'ān, Chányīshī Fúyán Yòu, came to her residence.
When she reached the age of twenty, he went to consult Kōngshān. One day, Shān asked him, "Have you ever seen Zhào?"
"What do you say? The scholar raised his voice and said, "No. Shanshan then ceased speaking. He would often say to others, "This man is one who has returned for a second birth.
The scholar once served as the Commander-in-Chief of Jianghuai and, while stationed in Jiading, Suzhou, he built Yongshou Temple to welcome monks from all quarters.
Jianghe Yongming’s *Mountain Dweller Poems* and other verses by Chan Master Shou all transcend the ordinary and surpass the mundane.

Regarding the incense offering on the anniversary of Bodhidharma’s death, he said: "Coming from the West, you did not fulfill the Emperor of Liang’s intent; Going back to the West, you carried away only a single sandal.
If one speaks of wondrous function or supernatural powers, Who among true patch-robed monks would even count you? Nine years facing the wall—seeking only to leave the stage."
Having received one person who was moreover without arms, his robes and bowl were passed down to Lu Neng. From this point on, the entanglements have grown without end;
the transgressions fill the heavens, while not a drop of the original source remains. Today, seven hundred and eighty-six years later, we encounter the anniversary of the memorial service.
Which descendant would not feel this pain to the very marrow of their bones? With a single incense burner and a single bowl of tea, we repay his kindness.
Yet this is precisely what constitutes ingratitude. I wish to raise my fist to show it to you, but pity that he has already lost his front teeth.

Master Huazang, a successor in the lineage of the Chan Master of Yangshan Jinzhi Ling in Suzhou, spoke to the assembly at the Iron Cage Hermitage of Master Nian: "The entrustment at Vulture Peak has spread throughout the world."

A thicket of entanglements. The single transmission of Shaoshi has become a den of right and wrong in all quarters. To settle the mind and repent of offenses, one must break open the lacquer bucket and restore its brilliance.
To transmit the Dharma and pass on the robe, one merely exerts oneself in vain by haggling over the price of stagnant wares.

Under Linji’s staff, the true eye is opened; beneath his fist, the way of life is revealed. In Caodong’s brocade curtains, mandarin ducks are embroidered—a sight travelers find difficult to behold. Yunmen...
These three phrases can be discerned. First: "The arrowhead pierces the vast void. Within the Dharma-eye, the great earth, mountains, and rivers are all wondrous functions.
In the Mañjuśrī-vajra-seal of Muzhou and Yangshan, there is no seam or crack; it stands like a sheer cliff, devoid of center or periphery.
Behold: the world is clear and peaceful; why needlessly create complications? Today, Jinyin shall resolve this public case for you all. Look, look! [He raises his staff.]
Draw a single line. The waves of the four seas are stilled and the dragon sleeps in peace; the clouds of the nine heavens are clear and the crane flies high.
Again, he cites Sansheng’s words: "When I meet people, I come forth; when I come forth, I do not act for others. Xinghua said: "When I meet people, I do not come forth;
when I come forth, I immediately act for others. The verse says: Who says the family style is divided into two sides? A single staff, two...
People are led astray. Cease contemplating the manner in which a thousand peaks soar toward the clouds; it is better to gaze upon the Milky Way falling from the Nine Heavens.

A verse on the dialogue concerning Śāriputra entering the city and Candrottarā leaving the city: Leaving the city and entering the town, the two meet face to face; who says their paths are different as they come and go?
Turning one's head to look back at the Terrace of Nirvāṇa, throughout the nine provinces and four seas, there is but the single wind of the Dharma.
Chan Master Mengshan Deyi of Mount Sheng in Songjiang Prefecture was a dharma successor of Chan Master Ningshan Huanshan. He was the son of the Lu family of Gaoyuan.
Initially, he studied under Chengtian Gu-chan, who instructed him to contemplate the "Mu" (No) koan of Zhaozhou. One day, Gu-chan asked: "When a deceased monk passes away, where does he go?"

He departed. The Master was at a loss for a response. Fei began to investigate the matter deeply. Later, when the Head Seat entered the hall and dropped a censer box, making a sound, Fei attained sudden enlightenment.
He composed a verse, saying: "The path of worldly ambition is exhausted; I have trodden over the waves until they become water. Transcending all, the old Zhaozhou!"
His face and features were exactly as they are. He went to visit the great masters Xueyan, Tui-geng, and Xu-zhou.
Xu-zhou asked, "If it is not the mind, not the Buddha, and not a thing, what is it? The Master replied, "All that I offer is the truth.
Again, he asked, "What was the intent behind Nanquan’s killing of the cat? The Master replied, "Opening the belly and emptying the heart. Xu-zhou said, "Zhaozhou wears straw sandals."
[Zhaozhou] asked, "If you go out wearing shoes, what then? The Master said, "Both hands and feet are exposed.

One day, in the meditation hall, Zhizhou asked, "When snow covers the thousand mountains, why is the solitary peak not white? The Master said, "It is a separate world. Zhizhou praised him greatly and urged him to visit Huanshan.
Huanshan asked, "The luminous, tranquil illumination pervades the sands of the Ganges; is this not Zhang Zhuo’s verse?"

As soon as these words were spoken, the Master was about to respond when Mount Shan shook his majestic presence and let out a single shout. At that moment, the Master was suddenly relieved and enlightened. One day, Mount Shan raised the koan:
"The saying goes, 'Deeply reclining in the clouds, not facing the court. Why have you come here? The Master replied, "When the Way prevails in the state, one appears.
Mount Shan deeply approved. Later, he served as the First Seat under Chuantian Jue’an. Subsequently, he lived in seclusion at Xiuxiu Hermitage by the Lotus Lake Bridge.

The student said, "When you speak thus, is there still a point where you benefit others? The Master said, "There is. The student asked, "Ultimately, which phrase is it?
The Master said, "Ask from the beginning. The student asked, "What is 'the ten directions gathering together'?

The Master said, "Dragons and snakes are intermingled; ordinary people and sages meet. The student asked, "What is 'each and every one learning non-action'? The Master said, "Swallowing with the mouth."

The Buddha’s and Patriarchs’ eye covers heaven and earth. [A monk] asked, "What is the field for selecting Buddhas? The Master said, "Ten thousand miles east and west, eight thousand miles south and north.

[The monk] asked, "What is it like to return home having passed the examination with an empty mind? The Master said, "Moving one's countenance to reveal the ancient road, yet not falling into the trap of silent stillness.
[The monk] said, "If that is so, then every word reveals the ultimate truth, and every sentence flows toward the source. The Master said, "How is it with you?"
[The monk] perceived it upon seeing [the master]. The monk shouted. The Master said, "This too is like swinging a club at the moon. [The monk] said, "Let this matter rest for a moment.
But as for today’s gathering of the ten directions at Xifeng, where the field for selecting Buddhas has opened—what auspicious signs are there ultimately? The Master said:
"The mountains, rivers, and great earth, and the myriad phenomena in their array—sentient and insentient alike—all attain Buddhahood.

[The student] asked, "If all have already attained Buddhahood, why is it that this student does not attain Buddhahood? The Master said, "If you were to attain Buddhahood, how could you cause the great earth to attain Buddhahood?"
[The monk] asked, "Ultimately, where does the student's fault lie? The Master said, "South of Xiang and north of Tan.
[The monk] asked, "Do you permit the student to repent? The Master said, "Prostrate yourself. The monk prostrated. The Master said, "A lion bites;

a Korean hound chases after clods of earth. He addressed the assembly: "The hundreds of thousands of Buddhas, the ancestral masters of successive generations, and even the old monks throughout the world..."
The Master struck the meditation seat once with his whisk and said, "Everyone here has fallen into a pit or a ditch. Is there anyone who can leap out?
He struck it again and said, "Sixty kalpas in three lifetimes. He then ascended the hall and said, "The realms of boundless lands are not separated by so much as a hair’s tip;
ten ages of past and present never depart from this very moment of thought. Just like this..."
Every day this mountain monk sleeps crosswise or upright within Zhanggong Cave, sometimes singing and sometimes chanting. Do you all know this?
Every day you all walk east and west within the field where Buddhas are selected, sometimes angry and sometimes joyful. Does this mountain monk know this?
If both sides were to know it, one could not avoid being split into many bodies to be pounded in mortars, or having one’s tongue pulled out and plowed with a furrow.
If both parties do not know, Śākyamuni will surely fold his hands and Maitreya will take refuge [in you]. Why is this so?
Have you not heard it said that the single word "knowing" is the gateway to all calamities? Ascending the hall, he said: "The myriad dharmas return to the One;

All people who eat gruel and rice do so within this; those who defecate and urinate do so within this;
walking, standing, sitting, and lying down—even a single movement or stillness—is entirely within this.
If you can recognize this, Master Bodhidharma would serve as nothing more than a foot-washing slave for you. If you do not recognize it, then as for the morning and evening meals—take them!
What is there to eat? *Chan*. Opening the retreat, I ascend the hall: the great limit is ninety days; the small limit is seven days.

Within the coarse is the subtle; within the subtle is the dense. Dense upon dense, without interval, not even a speck of dust can stand. At this very moment, it is like silver mountains and iron walls.
To advance is to have no door; to retreat is to lose it. It is like falling into a ten-thousand-fathom deep pit, with precipices and thorns on all four sides.
You must, as a fierce hero, turn yourself upside down in one stroke and leap out. If you hesitate for even a single thought, even a Buddha cannot save you.
This is the most supreme, mysterious gate. I exhort everyone to exert their full strength. Although this mountain monk—

Adjusting his robe over his left shoulder, he performed a woman’s bow and said: "It is not merely a matter of blending with the light and sharing the dust;
it is to avoid one another being left at a standstill. The Master once gave this instruction in his room: "A person of ultimate penetration is fundamentally liberated from birth and death.

why, then, is it obscured by a single cloud? Every person has a shadow that never leaves them for even a single step;

Their conversation did not harmonize, and he closed his door, refusing to receive him. Few who were not endowed with the eye that penetrates the barrier would not have retreated upon seeing the precipice.
In the year Xinmao, Qu, the Director of the Imperial Household at Hesha, came to the mountain to pay his respects and offered a vast estate to support the assembly.

The Master firmly declined and would not accept it. Qu petitioned the authorities, whereupon a separate Chan monastery named Dajue was established on Lotus Peak; it was planned to be [supported] annually.
He entered into the permanent endowment of the monastery and requested that his Dharma heir, Master Yong, take charge of monastic affairs. The Master had suffered from a chronic stomach ailment;
just as Yong came to visit him, the Master entrusted him with his final instructions. At dawn on the first day of the twelfth month, he ascended the seat and addressed the assembly, saying:
For thirty years at West Peak, I have vainly discoursed on Prajñā; my offenses fill the heavens.
In the end, there is one phrase that I dare not burden you all with—I shall take it upon myself alone. Is there anyone among you who knows its ultimate destination? After a long silence, he said:
"A difference of a hair’s breadth, and heaven and earth are separated. Between the hours of Chen and Si, he spoke another verse: "Coming, I do not enter death."
Guankou. He did not emerge from the "Deadly Barrier" (Sīgguān). An iron snake burrowed into the sea; Mount Sumeru was toppled. All became still and silent.
His final instruction was to enshrine his entire body in a stupa at the Deadly Barrier. He was fifty-eight years old and forty-three years since his ordination.
Chan Master Niuhe Chiding of Lingyun in Hengzhou was a native of the Wang family from Baxi in Taituo.
He was the ninth-generation descendant of the late Song Dynasty Minister Zhi. From childhood, he was austere and upright, possessing aspirations beyond the mundane world.

At the age of thirty, he visited Ken’an of Xifeng to have his hair shaved and there heard the essential tenets of the separate transmission. Subsequently, he went to rely upon Xueyan, serving as a stable-hand at the granary.

He practiced the dhūta austerities. One day, Dayuan addressed the assembly, saying, "Brothers, when you are practicing the Way, if for seven days and nights you maintain an uninterrupted single thought yet find no point of entry, then chop off my head to make a ladle for excrement. The Master understood this silently;
he exerted himself with diligent vigor and, suffering from dysentery, he forbade all medicinal decoctions and liquids, maintaining only right mindfulness with his eyes fixed [on the object].
He did not blink for seven days. At midnight, he suddenly perceived that the mountains, rivers, and the great earth throughout the entire realm were like snow;
his majestic body was such that heaven and earth could not contain it. After a short while, hearing the sound of wood being struck, he attained sudden enlightenment.

Sweat flowed from his entire body and his illness was cured. In the morning, he went to the abbot’s quarters to relate this experience. Master Yan questioned him repeatedly, and subsequently appointed him as...
One day, Master Shouyan ascended the hall and raised the case of a deceased monk, asking, "The monk is dead and has been cremated; where has he gone?
He then provided his own verse in response: "Mountains, rivers, and the great earth—all fully reveal the body of the Dharma King. At these words, the Master’s doubts were completely cleared away.
He immediately stepped forward from the assembly, prostrated himself, and said, "Just now, the Master expounded upon Prajñā, startling the stone lion in front of the Dharma Hall!"
The Master laughed and danced without ceasing. Yankuan said, "Try to say something. The Master replied: "Spring returns beyond the kalpas and all things wither;

mountains, rivers, and the great earth are without a speck of dust. How can the Dharmakāya, which transcends all, be pointed out? It makes the blue-eyed barbarian of the Western Heaven laugh to his downfall."
Yanguan struck the meditation desk with his staff and said, "Mountains, rivers, and the great earth—there is not a speck of dust. What is this? The Master made a gesture as if overturning it.
Yanguan laughed and said, "One win, two wins. One day, while entering the room for instruction, Yanguan said, "Bring forth a single phrase from the point of intimacy.

[The Master] said, "This is not worth half a coin. Yǎn said, "A talkative fellow. While Yǎn was inspecting the hall, the Master lay down with his body wrapped in a paper quilt.
Yǎn summoned him to the abbot’s quarters and said in a stern voice, "I am inspecting the hall and you are sleeping.

In the twenty-fifth year of the Zhiyuan era, he arrived at Taoyuan Mountain in Lincun County; finding its seclusion and depth pleasing, he [decided to stay].
He possessed a disposition for seclusion and reclusion. Not long after, County Magistrate Chen Gong and his subordinates entered the mountains to seek the Way;

they all followed him in performing the rites of disciples. He subsequently propagated the lineage of Xueyan extensively. On the fifteenth day of the first month in the seventh year of the Dade era, he demonstrated entry into *nirvāṇa*.
He was sixty-four years of age and had twenty-six years of monastic seniority (*varṣa*). His entire body was enshrined in a stupa thirty *li* north of the temple at Sha.
