The Master said, "Fan Kuai trampled at the Hongmen Gate. The Abbot prepared a vegetarian feast and ascended the hall. Yunmen, while eating a steamed bun, bit into the Emperor.
Regarding the nostrils of Śakra: when Yunfeng ate *bǎotòu* (steamed noodles), he bit into the tongue of Kātyāyanīputra.
When everyone goes up to the hall for the two daily meals—to eat porridge or to eat rice—how should one act?
Only when you suddenly bite through a piece of iron-sour stuffing will you realize that the nostrils of Śakra are precisely the tongue of Kātyāyanīputra, and the tongue of Kātyāyanīputra is...
This is because Śakra’s nostrils do not see the path; the omniscience of all-knowledge is pure, non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
(He lets out a shout. I request the head monk to ascend the hall. Excellent! Strike the board three times; let all who know the Way come to investigate.
Since you well understand the proper timing, I shall not repeat myself. When the ancients spoke thus, it was much like pressing down upon—
The ox-head eats grass; Yunfeng, however, is not so. How excellent! With three strikes of the board, he draws back his feet and ascends the meditation seat.

His backbone is cast of forged iron; he has passed through the patriarchs' barrier. In a single breath, he turns the entire Great Canon of Teachings; with his back turned, he plucks away Mount Sumeru.
When the mind is sought through the seven inquiries, no mind can be found; when the seeing is analyzed through the eight returns, no seeing can be returned. A dream...
Entering the celestial palace, he has not yet awakened; the golden cock crows atop the jade balustrade. Returning to the hall after his tour of transformation, he says:
"Where there is a Buddha, do not dwell; where there is no Buddha, pass by swiftly. Even when meeting people three thousand miles away, do not speak of this mistakenly."
The Old Man of Zhaozhou was much like one who, while washing himself by the bridge, clutches the pillar for support and lets go of the mooring rope as he steps onto the boat.
This mountain monk has been abroad for over forty days; where there is a Buddha, I have pierced his divination charts with a awl, and where there is no Buddha, I have likewise put him to the test.

I have traversed three prefectures and five counties, and whenever I encountered someone, I would deliberately misquote them. It is simply that the land is vast and the people are few—there is no one who truly understands.
Few are those who do so. Plucking the willow blossoms—plucking the willow blossoms. Suddenly remembering the green mountains, he returns; wishing to behold the dusty world, he descends again.

Entering the hall [he said]: "The nature of awakening is wondrously luminous; original awakening is luminously wondrous. This cuts off the life-root of the patch-robed monks and clears away the single aperture above.
A cowhide drum is stretched upon a pillar; the pillar shrieks and squeals. Those with ordinary ears do not hear it. All...
The Sage laughs with "he-he. The void leaps and dances through the three stages; the *wei-dou* kettle for brewing tea is not the same as a *xiao*. [He] ascends the hall.
"Three catties of hemp. "A dried dung pellet. "A wax figure, an ice goose, and snow protection. "The cat has the merit of drinking blood;

the tiger has the virtue of raising the dead. "Zhaozhou personally saw Old Nanquan. "Linji was not yet a 'white-handed thief' (a master thief who takes without leaving a trace). "Ascending the hall at Qingmiao Monastery.
"It is easy for the Bodhisattva Sadāprarudita to sell his heart and liver to study Prajñāpāramitā; it is difficult to break open a single atom."
To extract a great sutra scroll from [a single atom] is difficult; to extract a great sutra scroll by breaking open a single atom is easy.
To condense the sutras of the great trichiliocosm into a single atom is difficult. A handful of water can swell into waves that reach the heavens;
a single basketful of earth can form a mountain nine *zhang* high. It is neither difficult nor easy. The green mountains forever accompany the white clouds.

Yunxian went to the lecture hall of Yuwang Monastery. For many years he has dragged the plow and pulled the harrow; his nostrils reach toward the heavens and cannot be pierced. His karmic debts remain as before, impossible to escape;
once again he blows his iron flute as he passes through Ningbo. On the eighth day of the twelfth month, he ascended the hall and said:

"I observe that all sentient beings throughout the great earth possess the wisdom, virtue, and marks of a Tathāgata; it is only because of deluded thoughts and attachments that [they do not realize it]."

"One cannot realize it. Thus spoke Old Śākyamuni; it is much like a gnat building a nest upon the eye-lashes of a mosquito, standing at a crossroads and shouting at the top of its voice, "The land is vast and the people few;
those who meet one another are scarce. To examine this closely, he is but a fellow who eats wine dregs. Entering the hall, he raised the following case: A monk asked Wuzu...
The Great Canon of Teachings is a "cutting foot" (a rhyming suffix). I wonder what word it cuts? The Patriarch said: *Balaranya*.
Master Ying’an asked Miam, “What is the True Dharma Eye? Miam replied, “A broken sand pot. The Master said, “Fujian and Sichuan share the same custom;
there is a worm in the belly. He ascended the hall and said: “Do not seek it in the Buddha; do not seek it in the Dharma; do not seek it in the Sangha.”
The lantern laughs; the pillar nods its head. Yunmen brings forth a sesame cake; Touzi says, “Oily, oily.
Wrapping ten thousand strings of cash around one’s waist, riding a crane up to Yangzhou. Entering the hall, he said: “A fragrant breeze comes from the south;
the halls and pavilions grow cool. Old Miaoxi mistakenly took a donkey’s saddle for his father’s chin, bringing trouble upon how many people!
Just now, I was merely speculating. Do you know where the Buddhas emerge? "The Yellow River clears only once every three thousand years. [He plants his staff. He descends from the seat.
Ascending the hall, he says: "In the morning they are in a hurry; in the evening they are in a hurry. The alms bowl opens its mouth only to devour emptiness.
Nanquan smashed the cooking pot; Ganji bowed before the steamer. [He strikes the whisk. Ten thousand miles, eight..."
The Ninth Month. A northwest wind blows across the body. At the summer retreat’s small *śāmaṇa* (sermon), Langye pointed out five illnesses;
Xi-yuan deliberated on two errors. A well-frog is insufficient for speaking of the Eastern Sea; a summer insect cannot be spoken of ice and frost.
If one is a swift falcon soaring through the void, one should seize the moment; a fish exhausted in a shallow pond merely exerts itself in vain against the waves. Therefore, from—

Whether they be Buddhas above, Patriarchs, or the elder monks of the world, there is none who has not attained Equal and Perfect Enlightenment upon mountains of knives and trees of swords, or amidst cauldrons of boiling water and glowing embers, in order to deliver sentient beings. Yet, if I, this mountain monk, look at it from my own perspective, it is like a weight dipped in vinegar.
(He lets out a shout. Ascending the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat: At the beginning of autumn and the end of summer, you brothers go here and there.
Go! It is like a strong man extending his arm, requiring no external force; it is like a lion roaming, seeking no companion.
This is because beneath the heels of every person there is a living path that reaches through the heavens.
The Buddhas of the three periods, the six generations of patriarchs, and all the old monks of the world walk hand-in-hand with you. Have you not seen how Master Yunmen questioned Dongshan?
"What have you recently left? "Chadu. "Where were you for the summer retreat? "In Hunan. "When did you leave Baoci? "On the twenty-fifth day of the eighth month.
Baizhang said, "I grant you three blows of the staff. The next day, Dongshan went up to the abbot’s quarters and asked, "Yesterday I received the Master's three blows of the staff;
I do not know where my fault lay. Baizhang said, "You rice-bag! You people from Jiangxi!"
Hunan went off in this very manner. At these words, Shanshan attained great enlightenment. Yunmen brought forth his sky-reaching long sword, its divine edge formidable and unyielding;
Dongsan dared to charge at it with his bare body through those white blades.
At such a moment, what is it like? The golden crow pecks through the crystal shell; the jade hare pushes open the gate of the azure sea. Formerly, Fenyang had this:
There are ten criteria for examining a student. Master Gulin composed ten verses on this theme, and the Master (Xuedou) followed suit by composing verses in response to Gulin.

Regarding the discernment of the correct from the deviant, he said: "Households above and below are as numerous as hemp seeds; Those who come must be taught to test what is correct and what is deviant.

To seize tigers and oxen within the flash of a stone-light, And to distinguish dragons and snakes within the shadow of a lightning-flash— Lest one be reckless and superficial, saying: 'Afflictions are True Suchness.'"
Do not be reckless; fear that you may be muddled regarding ignorance and Buddha-nature. When the Great Spirit raises his hand, it does not take much to split apart the thousand-fold Mount Taihua.
When clever discernment is not true, it is said: "The eight returns that distinguish seeing are fundamentally not delusions;

the seven locations that seek the mind mistakenly take the real as false. How could my wisdom lack the power of samādhi? Ānanda speaks in vain of his kinship with the heavens. To attain its full function—
He said: "The Lion’s Seat by the West River stands before the gate; at the mere suggestion of it, one's soul and spirit are struck with terror.

A single scroll of paper money, along with wine and meat—idle spirits and wild ghosts vie with one another to rush toward it. He further proposed: "What was obtained from Mount Jing is not fine jade."
Seeking it in the vermilion waters, it is not a pearl; with a single blow, everything is shattered. The old man from the Western Heaven has no beard or mustache.

One who discerns the master says: When a thunderclap shakes the earth, it is hard to avoid; when the blazing sun shines upon the great thousandfold world, there is nothing else for swordsmen to encounter but to polish their three-foot-long ancient Dragon Spring blades. One who recognizes the sharp point of the wit says: This is the staff of Deshan.
Below, life and death are fully manifested; within Linji’s shout, host and guest are distinguished. To hesitate for a moment is to be ten thousand miles from Baiyun;
at Lantian, Li General was suspected of being killed. Within these words, Mingzhen said: "A whole, round phrase suddenly emerges before one's eyes;
press down the clouds and investigate it with care. The footless immortal kicks one in the chest; the wordless youth speaks incessantly. — Xianzong.
It is said: "Mastery of both the school and its teachings, with body and function fully complete; he hurls forth the bramble-bush and the golden circle.
Behold those who cannot swallow it through—vainly acting as direct descendants of Yangqi. In praise of the Master’s skillful means: "Few know his 'white-thief' hand;
An old, ancient fellow with hair growing on his wooden teeth. How could his limbs ever bend outward? He turns a broom upside down to draw [the circle]."

The Eyebrows of a Silkworm Moth. The general verse says: A patch-robed monk must penetrate the pivot of the Patriarchs. The Great Way stands majestic, reaching through the nine avenues. The Ten Sages and Three Worthies clarify this principle;
The myriad phenomena of the universe revolve upon the spiritual axis. Seize the ceremonial tablet from the hands of the stone statue;
Pluck the pearl from beneath the chin of the black dragon. Defeat Fenyang and Poyun; At the three-tiered Dragon Gate, they transform into dragons.

During the Zhizheng era, he was commissioned by imperial decree to preside over a grand Water and Land Assembly at Mount Jinshan. The Emperor ordered him to ascend the seat and preach the Dharma, and specially bestowed upon him imperial incense and silk brocades.
In his later years, he lived in seclusion in a hermitage named "Pine and Moon" (Songyue) and styled himself the "Elder Pine and Moon" (Songyue Weng).
Chan Master Nanchu Yue of Mount Jingshan in Hangzhou was a native of Longxing. He ascended the hall and said: "To awaken to the Way through sound; to clarify the mind through form.
Suddenly he took up his staff, saying, "This is form," and struck the ground once. "This is sound. "Everyone here sees this and hears this.
But tell me, which is the mind that clarifies? Which is the Way that is awakened to? He let out a shout.
To covet another's single grain of rice is to lose half a year’s worth of provisions. He was posthumously bestowed the imperial title of Chan Master Foci Faxi (Buddha-Love Dharma-Joy).

Chan Master Yuejiang Zongjing of Jingshan in Hangzhou, a disciple of Chan Master Yin of Shuanglin, was the son of the Ni family of Lanxi. He recited the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* until he reached the passage beginning with "As..."
The finger pointing at the moon caused him to have a sudden realization. He went to visit Zheng’an of Shuanglin, who asked, "How do you understand Huangbo’s striking Linji?
The Master replied, "It is like pressing a cow's head down so it must eat grass. Later, when he appeared in the world at Jingshan, as he was about to pass away, he wrote a verse:
"A guest at the gate of the Patriarchs, Opens his mouth to discuss non-arising. I, old and worn, understand nothing at all; At midday, I strike..."
At the third watch, he passed away peacefully.
Chan Master Minji Jiaohui of Baoning in Jinling was a native of Wuxing. He received the Dharma from Chan Master Xibai Jin and subsequently emerged [as his successor].
He was a paragon of auspicious virtue in the world, like that of Xihe during the Xiangfu era. He subsequently shared the teaching seat at Tianjie Monastery and later presided over Baoning.
Song Wenxian Gong Lan once composed the "Record of the Chongmo Chamber" for him.
At that time, Chan Master Xiyu (Yi), known as Jingci Fojian Jian’an, was a successor of Chan Master Anfu. He was the son of the Li family of Jiahe.
At the age of seventeen, he entered the monastic order under Master Wanshou Tianyu Jing. Later, when Tianyu resided at Xihu in Lin’an, the Master attended him there.
While traveling, the conditions within his quarters did not harmonize with him. In a fit of indignation, he went to Lingyin Temple to visit Shiyuan (Shi’an).

Shi’an asked, “Where have you come from? The Master replied, “Jiangxi. Shi’an asked, “Have you ever seen the top-knot of the Great Master Mazu? The Master said, “Seeking the old kernel inside a peach pit for a thousand years—what kind of thing is that?
Shi’an nodded in approval and ordered him to reside in the Zhemu (Picking Trees) Hall. Later, because of the phrase “the dog has no Buddha-nature,” [he had a further realization].
Xinghua had a doubt regarding a dialogue and requested further instruction from Chan Master An. An said, "When Cold Spring flows upstream, I will tell you.

One day, he suddenly attained realization and went to the abbot’s quarters, saying, "Cold Spring is flowing upstream! An asked, "What have you seen? The Master replied, "A thousand peaks lose their momentum and rest at the edge of the mountains;
ten thousand streams return their sound and vanish into the sea. An gave a shout and said, "You are just spinning empty tales!"

He said to Han, "Thirty years from now, I shall depart, having lost my integrity. The Master then shook out his sleeves and left. Later, he resided at Chongfu Temple in Hangzhou and subsequently moved to Wanshou Temple.

During the Yongle era, he was summoned to assist in compiling the Great Canon; in response to the imperial decree, he attended to the task. Upon its completion, an edict appointed him as the abbot of Jingci Temple.
In the Renzi year of the Xuande era, he suddenly said to the assembly, "I am going. He ordered them to bathe him and change his robes, then wrote this verse:
"Mount Sumeru in a single fist; the great ocean in a single mouth. The sea dries up and the mountains crumble; the crow flies and the hare runs. Sitting upright, he passed away in stillness.
Chan Master Jingjie Dingyan of Linggu Monastery in Jinling was a successor of Chan Master Tanyue of Tianjie Monastery. He was a native of Wuxing.

Having gone to Tianjie to study under Jueyuan, Jueyuan questioned him regarding the karmic cause and condition of the exploding wooden箍 (gū) on a water bucket. As the Master hesitated, Jueyuan said in a stern voice, "It is already eight *kè* late!"
Upon hearing these words, the Master attained great enlightenment. At the beginning of the Hongwu era, he was summoned by imperial decree to reside at Linggu Monastery.

Addressing the assembly, he cited Changqing’s saying: "In general, it seems today the old barbarian has hope," and Baofu’s saying: "In general, it seems today the old barbarian has lost all hope. The Master offered this verse:

"Displaying the strategic maneuvers with full frankness, there is no need for boasting; To suppress or to uplift belongs fundamentally to those of the authentic lineage. The waves of Caoxi are like..."

[The two] are similar. How could there be descendants as numerous as rice and hemp? There exists a continuous carving of the *Lianzhu songgu* (Linked Pearl Verses on Ancient Cases) circulating within the monastic community.

(Master Yaoguangxiao, the Lesser Preceptor, inscribed a eulogy for the Master’s portrait, saying: "To see Dingyan through this is like mistaking a locust tree for a willow; not to see Dingyan through this is like mistaking the constellation Chen for the Big Dipper. If this were so, how then would one see Dingyan?

He takes the vast void as his measure and the serene autumn waters as his spirit. In speaking, he speaks without speaking; in hearing, he hears without hearing. His conduct is as pure as frost; his countenance is as warm as spring. He presides over an extraordinary and great monastery, reverently upholding [the Dharma] beyond..."

His great and profound grace reaches everywhere, no matter how distant; his virtue is never solitary, for it finds its neighbors. Alas! This truly makes him the rightful grandson of the Dragon-Soaring Xun of the Great Middle Way.
Chan Master Tianrong Ziran Zixing of Mount Yunyang in Mingzhou was a dharma successor of Chan Master Le of the Heavenly Realm. He was a native of the Han family of Yuyang.
He left the household life at Huizhao Hermitage on Hongxi Creek in Liyang and took Preceptor Huikai as his teacher. One day, Huikai asked him about his parents.
"Before you were born, what was that which is your original face? From then on, I harbored this doubt within my breast for seven years.
During this time, I engaged in earnest study and mutual stimulation with Jincheon Chaoan I-hwan (Sengbok); the two gentlemen's efforts contributed the most.
One day, Chaoan raised the koan, "The phrase with no phrase is like a vine leaning against a tree," and questioned me. As I was about to deliberate upon it, Chaoan—
He struck him across the spine. The Master was so incensed that he did not sleep all night. At dawn, he suddenly heard the sound of a fire-stirring stick striking wood;
he was instantly and completely enlightened. He said to the hermitage attendant, "The case from last night must be settled with you today.
As the attendant gripped his staff and asked, "Where does this phrase lead? before he could finish speaking, the Master snatched the staff from his hand and snapped it into two pieces.

He threw himself out the window and said, "Burn elsewhere! Then he went straight into the hall. Hearing this, Woho came specifically to ask, "I am glad that Brother Xing has completed his great matter.
The Master shouted, "Thieves do not strike the homes of the poor. One day, he asked Anzhu, "Are the meaning of Chan and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different?
Anzhu replied, "In autumn, yellow leaves fall from the trees; in cold weather, one digs the earth."
[Regarding the phrase] "The stove," the Master said, "For now, I shall not question him. Later, he visited Tianjie Quanshi.

Within the hall, [the Master] recounted the incident, saying, "In years past, I once asked a certain teacher whether the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings were the same or different.

He replied: 'Autumn trees shed yellow leaves; on a cold day, dig a stove in the ground. Today, I beg the Venerable Master to provide a definitive judgment. Quanshi said, "I am an old man who has been ill for many years."
His arms were weak; leaning on his staff by the bedside, he rested it against the wall. The Master said, "There are those who do not agree with you, Reverend, speaking thus.
The Abbot picked up his staff and struck him, saying, "Wait until the eyes of the pillar open of themselves. He then hurled an iron caltrop directly at the Master's face.
The Master then prostrated himself. Later, he appeared in the world at Puguang Monastery in Li. In the fifteenth year of the Hongwu era, he moved to Changzhou.
Yongqing was selected by public decree to reside at Shushan in Fuzhou, and later received an imperial edict to serve as abbot of Tiantong.

A monk asked, "When an ox passes through a window frame, its horns, head, and four hooves have all passed through; why is it that the tail cannot pass? The Master said, "The bowl slipped off the mound.
The monk said, "If that is so, then the Great Huì of old is the Fólang of today. The Master said, "Do not mistake the six dragons."

Chengzuo visited his maternal uncle’s house. The uncle asked, “The Master has entrusted you with the essential point; how did matters proceed on your return journey? The Master replied, “One must urgently spit it out.
Ascending the hall, he said: “One is three, and three is one. Whether saintly or ordinary, they cannot be distinguished. The wooden man dons brocade robes; the stone woman’s elegance is swift.
She is accustomed to playing the stringless lute and can blow the holeless flute. Deep within the bottom of the sea...”
Walking along, he stands atop a high peak. The pillar comes forward to bow its head; empty space joins in with a clap. The myriad phenomena listen with bated breath.
Everyone laughs at a single toss. But tell me, what is it they laugh at? They laugh at the starving man inside the grain basket who refuses to open his own mouth to eat.
Even if you reach the thirty-third heaven, how can you ever dispel your original hunger and suffering?
Holding up his staff, he said, "Ho! Ho! and immediately descended from the seat. Ascending the hall, he said: "Today is the first day of the tenth month; the monks prepare for winter.
Stir the flames of the hearth, and do not ask further about firewood or charcoal. When thirsty, drink the soup of molten copper; when hungry, eat the rice of iron nails.
Does the assembly know that there is no thread in the bag to bind even an ant, and that the kitchen lacks even a grain of flour to attract a fly? He then reached out...
There is no room for indolence here. [The Master] struck his staff and descended from the seat. To thank the head officers, he ascended the hall:
"As soon as the whisk of hair was blown, the infinite Flower Treasury World manifested; with the golden mallet held in hand, all Buddhas and Tathāgatas were brought under control."
Shattering the tea bowls, the sound of gold and jade resounds everywhere. Carrying the leaking oil lamps, they illuminate the past and soar through the present.
With a staff of rabbit horns, one picks up the sun and moon of the great thousand-fold world; with a whisk of tortoise hair, one turns the Dharma wheel across kalpas of dust.
Do you see how the mountain of the Buddha-land leaps and bounds, smashing through the nostrils of all of you and blinding the eyes of all of you? *Hè!* (A shout)

"Ha! The spring breeze and summer rain arrive in their proper seasons; white peaches and pink blossoms open one after another. [He ascends the hall. "On this very day last year, I dwelt on Mount Laṅkā.
The fourfold assembly there rejoiced, yet they felt one person was missing here. On this very day this year, I dwell on Mount Buddhakṣetra.
The fourfold assembly here rejoices, yet they feel one person is missing there. [He strikes the whisk. "One body becomes infinite bodies."
The immeasurable body becomes a single body. When walking, one walks throughout heaven and earth; when sitting, one sits within all things.
What need is there to speak of east, west, south, north, other lands, or this world? Even if you examine it thus, you are still in the "transformed city.

But tell me, what is the phrase for the "Jewel City"? [He] then descended from the seat. Ascending the hall, he said: "Greed, anger, and ignorance are precept, concentration, and wisdom; precept, concentration, and wisdom are greed, anger, and ignorance."

Greed, hatred, and delusion; ignorance and the knowledge and vision of liberation; the knowledge and vision of liberation and ignorance. All sentient beings are the Buddhas; all Buddhas are all sentient beings.
The moon has fallen, yet there is no shadow on the mountain; the wind comes, and the trees make a sound. Within the great trichiliocosm there is no counterpart;
the incense burner stands amidst bustling activity. [The Master] lets out a shout and descends from his seat. Entering the hall: Today is the first day of the tenth month.
The patch-robed monks prepared charcoal and opened the furnace. You know the proper time and recognize the seasons; I do not concern myself with such matters as "it is," "it was," or "it shall be.
Before the emergence of Buddhas, there was already the decree of the wild weeds: "The pure wind flows freely, filling the imperial capital.
One day, several monks from the assembly of Master Ning Yifeng arrived. The Master asked, "Are you the disciples of Master Yifeng? The monks replied, "We are."
The Master asked, "May I ask about your family affairs? The monk replied, "I may. The Master said, "Wrong.
He asked again, "Before the mountains of Fu in Xia, three weeds and two trees roar like lions day and night. Is this the speech of One Peak? The monk replied, "It is.
The Master again said, "Wrong. The monk was speechless. The Master said, "How is it that you have received the five precepts yet do not uphold them? In his later years, he retired back to Puhua.
Guang. Chan Master Wuben Wenbian of Lingyin Monastery in Hangzhou, successor to Chan Master De of Jingci Monastery. He was a native of Dinghai in Siming and surnamed Xie. At the age of ten...
At age four, he left home at Wutai Temple in Jun County, where he shaved his head, received full ordination, and rigorously studied the Vinaya.
Hearing that Gufeng was flourishing in his teachings at Baoning, he went there to pay his respects. One day, Gufeng asked him, "I have heard you have recited the 'Ten Oxherding Verses' by Liangshan;
try reciting them for me. As the Master prepared to respond, Gufeng suddenly covered his mouth and said, "Where are the oxen? The Master replied, "I have already committed an offense."
"Master, the crops have ripened," [the monk] said. Feng replied, "Not yet; speak further. The Master covered his ears and departed. Feng marveled at this and appointed him as an attendant.
At that time, Master Zhongfang Lun was living in retirement at a new hermitage to the right of the temple; the Master went back and forth there to resolve his doubts and refine his understanding.
In the twenty-sixth year of the Zhizheng era, he opened a Dharma center at Jueyan in Gusu; there, Yibian became the successor to Gufeng.
During the Hongwu period, the Jingle Monastery in Yixing requested that the Master change the teaching from lecture-style Buddhism to Chan.

Shortly thereafter, by imperial decree, the Chan monastery of Jiangshan was moved to the east of Xiaoling, renamed Linggu, and the Master was commanded by the Imperial Edict to serve as its abbot under the supervision of the Chan Master Wuwai Zhongxi.
He occupied the first seat and served as a model for the assembly. In the twenty-eighth year of the Hongwu era, he was appointed to Lingyin Monastery, where he resided for five years.
One day, he manifested slight illness. When Master Hong of Mingshi Fantang went to inquire after him, he encountered the Master gasping for breath.
Hong said, "Zhaozhou said, 'All people are driven by the twelve hours; this old monk drives the twelve hours. What about you, Master?"
"How so? The Master straightened his body and said, "What do you call the twelve periods of the day? Hong said, "How can one help it when one is out of breath?
The Master let out a thunderous shout. He asked those around him, "What is today's date? They replied, "The twenty-seventh day of the second month."
He then took up his brush and wrote a verse, saying: "I am seventy-five years old; I enter nirvana without falling into birth and death.
I turn my body upon the back of empty space and knock over the small cloud that has flown hither. Having cast down his brush, he passed away in stillness.

His cremation left the cranial bone unbroken and yielded countless śarīra relics. His disciples, including Zongyan and others, collected the remains and enshrined them in an indestructible stupa at Shuanggui Monastery.
His fingernails and hair were divided and buried at Jingle.
Zhiyan Cheng Chan Master’s Dharma heir was Chan Master Shiyu of Wushi Jiefeng in Quzhou; he was a native of the Yu clan from Xi’an in the commandery. From childhood, he was fond of...
He paid homage at Buddhist stupas. At the age of twenty, he left his home to enter the monastic order at Xianjiao Temple in Lanxi, where he shaved his head and received full ordination.

He visited such eminent masters as Guya, Shimen, Duanya, and Zhongfeng, receiving their dharma instructions with deep reverence. He resided at Nanping for three years without crossing the threshold of his room.
At that time, Zhiyan was propagating the Way at Daci; the Master went there to visit him once again. Zhiyan raised [the topic of] the South...
"Spring-water is neither mind, nor Buddha, nor a thing; what is it? The Master was at a loss. Thereupon, he returned once more to Nanping.
One night, hearing a neighboring monk recite the *Song of Realizing the Way* (*Zhengdao ge*), he reached the line: "Neither eliminating delusive thoughts, nor seeking the truth.

Suddenly, he felt as if a heavy burden had been lifted. He then said: "The Buddha-dharma has always been right before one's eyes; it is people themselves who distance themselves from it. He immediately composed [a verse].
The verse says: Time and again we meet face-to-face, yet do not truly encounter one another; Having exhausted the mother’s anger, my vital strength is spent.
At midnight, suddenly forgetting the pointing finger, A red sun-wheel bursts forth from the void. He ran to see Zhiyan;
as soon as Yan saw him, he shouted, "Where have you come from, seeing gods and ghosts? The Master said, "Today I have caught the thief. Yan asked, "Where is the stolen goods?"
[The Master] was in his quarters. The Master then gave a shout. Xuyan said, "Neither opening the mouth nor closing the mouth is right; bring forth a phrase that goes beyond this.
The Master said, "Clearly manifest throughout the entire world, nothing is hidden. Xuyan picked up his bamboo staff, and the Master overturned the meditation seat.
Xuyan said, "You dare to come here and pull at the tiger’s whiskers! He struck him three times and appointed him as his attendant. Later, he appeared in the world [as a master].
He moved from Wushan in Li to Shixi in Guangde. On the day he opened the hall for teachings, a monk asked: "Having left Wushan Ridge far behind, you have come to Stone Creek Mountain.

To reveal the path for humans and devas—how does one pass through the Patriarch’s barrier? The Master said: "A dragon gives birth to a golden phoenix chick; it breaks through the azure lapis lazuli. The monk said:
"If that is so, then though we face each other, we do not recognize one another; yet from a thousand miles away, we may share the same wind."

The Master said, "A layered mountain pass. [The monk] asked, "Bodhidharma came from the West not to establish written words, but to point directly to the human mind so that one may see one's nature and become a Buddha.
Since he did not establish written words, how is it that they have been transmitted down to the present day?

The Master said, "In official matters, even a needle cannot pass; in private affairs, carriages and horses may travel through. [The monk] asked, "When you say 'pointing directly to the human mind,' which mind do you point to? The Master said, "Open your mouth and..."
[The student] said, "To see one's nature is to become a Buddha. Where does this nature reside? The Master said, "The Taihu Lake spans thirty-six thousand acres;
night after night, the moonlight shines brightly upon its waves. [The student] said, "I recall the Great Being Fu Daoshi saying:
'Empty-handed, he grasps a hoe; walking, he rides a water buffalo. People pass over the tangerine tree; the bridge flows, yet the water does not flow. What is the meaning of this?"

"What? the Master said. "Be careful not to miss it right before your eyes. The monk said, "In that case, when there is spirit, one adds to that spirit; even where there is no elegance, there is elegance.
The Master said, "A difference of a hair's breadth results in a gap as vast as heaven and earth. The monk said, "Let us set this matter aside for now.
I recall it being said in the sutras that a great wealthy elder is none other than the Tathāgata. Does this refer to [the state of] many kalpas?"

[The monk] came forward. "Is this a realization attained in this very life? The Master said, "The stream is deep where the flowers fall far away; the mountain is high where the tree shadows stretch long.
[The monk] said, "Today, the Layman Zhixin has donated his family wealth to establish a practice center at Shixi and invites the Master to reside there.
Is this the same as before, or is it different? The Master said, "When the lion roars, the grass turns red and green; when the elephant king..."
The place of practice is filled with the crimson of a hundred flowers. A monk asked, "If it is thus, what karmic fruit will be obtained?

The Master said, "Life after life one returns to the Buddha-ground; age after age one rejoices among humans and devas. Ascending the hall, he said: "The Great Way has no form; it is beyond names and transcends signs.

There is no need for cultivation or realization, nor does it involve verbal explanation. The seventeen hundred barriers of the patriarchs—look closely, and you will see they are nothing other than this very thing. Relying on others..."

This constitutes the gate of self-awakening that resolves obstacles. If you wish to sweep away all entanglements and sever all superficial displays, you must, at the very moment when the Yellow-Faced Old Man was about to hold up the flower, and before the golden-haired *dhūta* had yet smiled, overturn the meditation seat and shout to disperse the assembly.
Only then will you spare future descendants from having to resort to striking with staffs or shouting out commands.
Pointing with his hand and raising his fist, he manifested ten thousand forms and a thousand skills. Today, this mountain monk will not point east or draw west;
I shall directly deliver a message to you all. After a long silence, he said: "The heavens are high, and the myriad phenomena are in their proper order."
The ocean is vast, and the hundred rivers flow toward it. In the twelfth month of the third year of Hongwu, he manifested a slight illness.

He wrote a verse, saying: "Birth is fundamentally non-birth; extinction is fundamentally non-extinction. Casting off my hands, I go forth; under the bright moon of the heavens. Having set down his brush, he passed away.

Chan Master Nicui Zhishun of Jingci Monastery in Hangzhou was a successor of Chan Master Tianbao Shu. He was born into the Chen family of Ruian, Wenzhou. His mother venerated an image of the Great Master Zhiyi with great devotion.
One night she dreamed of a monk with a halo around his head who ascended the river current against the flow and said: [The text continues from here.]

"I shall be your son. Upon waking, she conceived. When the child was born, his excellent qualities were already fully formed; he possessed a transcendent aspiration for the life beyond the mundane world.
At the age of seven, he followed his uncle, the śramaṇa Huiguang, at the Chongxing Vihāra.

Upon reaching adulthood, he received full ordination and traversed the vast ocean of doctrinal meaning. Suddenly, he abandoned it all and went to Min to seek refuge with Tianguan, whereupon Tianguan rebuked him.

[The Master] said, "A true man does not merely vie with others in great monasteries; why should he confine his thoughts to such a narrow place? He withdrew and entered the *danguo* (guest quarters), whereupon he wept bitterly.
When the Abbot heard of this, he ordered him to attend the communal hall. From that time on, the Master stood firm like a wall ten thousand fathoms high, with no distinction between day and night.
After more than a month, while using the toilet, he saw a bitter gourd in the central garden, which triggered an awakening; he suddenly realized the entire earth.
Pingchen went to see Guankou to seek certification. Guankou said, "This is merely entering the gate; as for the next step upward, it is thousands of miles away.
Another half-year passed, and one day Pingchen suddenly spoke in a stern voice, saying to Guankou, "I have now seen Nanquan’s point of failure.
Guankou asked, "It is not mind, not Buddha, and not a thing—what is it? The Master replied, "The ground."
The roof was paved with bricks and covered with tiles. Guankai asked, "Where is Nanquan now? The Master replied, "A hawk has flown to Silla.
Guankai said, "Wrong. The Master also said, "Wrong. Guankai said, "Wrong, wrong. The Master bowed and withdrew. He was then appointed to keep the storehouse keys.

Shortly thereafter, he was ordered to share the seat [with the abbot] to preach the Dharma. When Guankai passed away, the Master succeeded him in leading the monastery's affairs. Not long after, he abandoned them.

He departed, passing through the Shanggan Pass and reaching Baiyang. He ascended Mount Kāśyapa, crossed the Yangtze River, and entered the Huai region to pay homage at the stupas of the various patriarchs.

Returning from Jianye to Zhejiang, he soon returned to Yongjia and established Bao'en Monastery in Ruian. He subsequently moved to become the abbot of Jiangxin, and later established Guiyuan in Pingyang.
The imperial court bestowed upon him the monastery’s plaque and a gold-embroidered *kāṣāya*, and conferred upon him the title "Buddha-nature Yuanbian."
Chan Master [Xingjiao]: When Yan Zhibuhua, the Chancellor, was stationed in Min, he invited the Master to reside at Dongchan Xuefeng Monastery.

At the beginning of the Hongwu era, an imperial edict summoned ten eminent monks of realized virtue to Mount Zhongshan to establish a dharma assembly. The Master responded to the summons and was commanded to ascend the seat and preach the Dharma.

The Emperor visited him in person, offering the utmost consolation and care. Upon returning south, he was appointed as the abbot of Jingci Temple. After six years, he was summoned back to the capital.
Suddenly manifesting a slight illness, he bathed, recited a verse, and passed away while seated.

Chan Master Bifeng Baolin of Mount Wutai was a dharma successor of Chan Master Jinyun Zhen. He was a native of Yongshou County in Qianzhou and belonged to the Shi clan, a prominent lineage of the district.

His parents were devoted to the practice of goodness; a śramaṇa had bestowed upon them an image of Avalokiteśvara, and before long, the Master was born. At the time of his birth, [the image] turned white...

A light filled the room, and his parents marveled at this. When he was only six years old, they ordered him to leave the household life. After receiving the tonsure, he traveled extensively through various lecture halls.
Suddenly, he sighed and said, "The studies of the Tripiṭaka are all like a finger pointing at the moon. He then changed his robes and went to pay his respects to Master Zhinaihuai in Jin-yun.
Day and night he applied himself with diligent effort. Once, while carrying a basket to gather vegetables, he suddenly sat motionless for three [periods].
At that moment, he suddenly awoke. Zhen asked, "Have you entered meditative concentration? The Master said, "Yes. Zhen asked, "What did you see?
The Master said, "I have attained realization. Zhen asked, "How is this realization? The Master held up a basket and showed it to him. Zhen said, "This is not it.
The Master set the basket on the ground and stood with his hands folded. Zhen said again, "This is not it. The Master then let out a shout. Zhen grabbed him by the chest and said, "Speak!"
The Master clenched his fist and struck him. Zhen said, "Not yet; this is merely a temporary cessation of worldly toil.

One must cause the path of the mind to be cut off and penetrate the Patriarchal Barrier before the Great Dharma can be clarified. From then on, the Master did not let his side touch the mat for three years.
One day, hearing the sound of wood being felled, his sweat fell like rain. He said, "The ancients said that they had a great awakening eighteen times and countless minor awakenings;
how could they have deceived me? Only today do I finally understand what occurred before birth. He immediately went to see Huizhen to seek certification.
Huizhen did not grant it. The Master overturned the meditation seat and left. The following day he saw Huizhen again, who was on the ground.
The Master drew a circle on the wall; the student brushed it away with his sleeve. The student drew another circle;
the Master drew a line across the circle and brushed it away. The student drew a third circle; the Master drew a cross within the circle and brushed it away.
The student drew yet another as before; the Master drew a swastika (*svastika*) in the corners of the cross and brushed it away.
Zhen drew thirty circular diagrams in total. The Master answered each one in detail. Zhen laughed heartily and said, "Are there not those in the world who have attained realization through study?
But how many can truly manifest such great functional power? He then conferred upon him the prediction of enlightenment and commanded him to go to Shuofang, where his Way would surely flourish.
Previously, while in meditative concentration, the Master had seen a mountain of exquisite beauty, with its tiered pavilions and towering halls."

The pavilion was resplendent with gold and lapis lazuli, and various bodhisattvas were practicing the Way within it. A person who had invited the Master there said, "This is Secret Demon Rock (Bimō Yán).

Why have you forgotten it so quickly while practicing the Way here? Later, as the Master was traveling to Mount Tai, he encountered on the road a woman with disheveled hair wearing tattered garments of five colors;
she walked slowly barefoot, followed by a black mastiff. The Master asked her: [...what she was doing...]

[The questioner] asked, "Where have you gone? He replied, "I have entered the mountains. The Master asked, "For what purpose have you entered the mountains? He replied, "I have done nothing at all. Having spoken, he vanished.
[The Master] knocked on those who had traveled with him, but none were to be seen. Some said he was a transformation-body (nirmāṇakāya) of Mañjuśrī.

Consequently, the Master established Lingjiu Hermitage on the mountain to await those yet to come. Monastics and laypeople, hearing of his reputation, flocked there from a thousand li away; the crowds often reached ten thousand. Upon his arrival—

He was summoned to the inner court during the intercalary month. It happened that one night during a great snowfall, a crimson light issued directly from the master’s quarters, piercing through to the heavens.
The Emperor marveled at this and bestowed upon him a gold-embroidered *kāṣāya*. The following year, when he prayed for rain, it fell immediately in response.

By imperial decree, he was granted the title of Great Zen Master Jigyo Wonyeom (Silent Illumination Perfect Enlightenment) and was summoned to reside at Haerin Temple. At the beginning of the Hongwu era, after the High Emperor ascended the throne, the following year—
When the Yan capital was pacified, an imperial decree summoned the Master to the capital to reside at Dàtiānjiè Temple. His exposition of the Dharma accorded with the Emperor’s wishes.

On the *xīnhài* day, a Universal Salvation Assembly (*pǔjì huì*) was established at Zhōngshān, and the Master was commanded to preside over its proceedings. The Emperor bestowed upon him *ípú* vegetarian fare and personally visited the site.

From his own hand, the Emperor granted a poem, bestowing such abundant favor and bounty. On the sixth month of the *rénzǐ* year, he bathed, changed his robes, and gathered the assembly to bid them farewell. His disciples...
He requested a verse, to which the Master replied: "The Tripitaka and the twelve divisions of the scriptures are but old paper; what use are my words?

He then sat upright and closed his eyes. His secular age was sixty-five and his monastic seniority fifty years. Upon cremation, his relics formed five colors, and both his teeth and tongue remained uncorrupted.

Chan Master Wuming Qianyan Yuanchang of Fulong in Wushang, Wuzhou, was a dharma successor of Chan Master Tianmu Ben. He was a native of Xiaoshan in Yue, born into the Dong clan.
At the age of seven, he followed his paternal uncle, the bhikṣu Tanguang, at Famen Monastery in Fuyang. At nineteen, he...

Having shaved his head and received full ordination, he studied the Vinaya at Lingzhi Monastery. During a time when the Chancellor was hosting a meal for the monastic community at the Prime Minister’s residence, the Master entered with the assembly.
Master Zhongfeng happened to be seated there; seeing the Master from afar, he called out to him and asked, "How do you conduct your daily practice?"
The Master said, "Recite the Buddha's name. Xuefeng asked, "Where is the Buddha now? The Master hesitated; Xuefeng rebuked him with a stern voice.
The Master prostrated himself and requested instruction on the essential points of the Dharma. Xuefeng gave him the koan of the dog having no Buddha-nature.

He lived in a thatched hut at Lingyin for three years, never letting his side touch the mat. One day, while at Wangting, he attained realization upon hearing the sound of sparrows. He immediately went to see Xuefeng.

He related his realization in detail, but the Master [Zhaozhou] rebuked him again. The teacher returned home in a fit of indignation. In the stillness of night, a rat suddenly overturned the cat’s food bowl;
as it fell to the ground, it made a sound. At that moment, he attained sudden enlightenment. He went back once more to question the Master, who said, "Why did Zhaozhou say 'no'?"
The Master said, "The rat eats the cat's meal. Fēng said, "Not yet. The Master said, "The vessel for the meal is broken. Fēng asked, "What is it like after it is broken?
The Master said, "Only when it is crushed into fine tiles. Fēng then smiled and was instructed, saying, "Guard and uphold this well yourself.

When the time arrives, its principle will manifest of itself. Having received these instructions, the Master went into seclusion at the Eastern Hermitage of Tiānlóng. Xiàoyǐn became the abbot of Zhōngzhú.

He was strongly recommended for appointment. The Imperial Preceptor of the Jiang-Zhe Provincial Administration, Prince Tuohan, who headed the Xuanzheng Yuan, also dispatched envoys to urge the Master to take up a monastic post.
The Master declined them all. Before long, the abbots of various mountains vied with one another to invite him;
realizing he could not be accommodated by the times, he took up his staff and crossed the Tiantai River to the east, arriving at Mount Fulong in Wushang.
Like a blue lotus, he planted his mendicant’s staff at the edge of the cliff and vowed, "If there is water in this mountain, I shall dwell here.
Immediately, a mountain spring overflowed, appearing the color of white milk. The Master then took up residence by a great tree; it was the tenth month of the Dingmao year of the Taiding era.
Previously, there had been a Chan temple on the mountain named Shengshou, which had been abandoned for a long time. When the Master entered the mountain, the local villagers...
Everyone dreamed that an extraordinary monk had arrived; they subsequently led one another through the thick undergrowth to search for him.

Finding the Master sitting in meditation, unmoving, each person offered food and drink. The prominent local clansmen, Lou Junru and Lou Jundi, joined forces to clear the land and construct a refined hermitage.
Later, based on its original name, it was developed into a great monastery (*mahāvihāra*). The imperial court thrice dispatched high-ranking ministers to bestow incense upon it.
He was conferred the honorary title of Chan Master Fohui Yuanjian Pujie (Buddha-Wisdom Perfect Mirror Universal Salvation) and granted a golden-embroidered dharma robe.

He asked, "What is the host within the guest? The Master said, "Sitting in the hall at noon tomorrow. He asked, "What is the guest within the host? The Master said, [as before].

The Master said, “He does not eat meat; he eats only mice. The monk asked, “How can a *shanzhishi* (a person of good knowledge) tolerate him?

He took his seat on the meditation platform. A monk asked, "What is the first phrase? The Master said, "To have a mouth like one who is mute.

The Master said, "When the 'array against the water' is complete, one’s valor and vigor increase. [The monk] asked, "What is it like when both the person and the environment are seized?

The Master said, "Even before a sharp blade, one remains ever level; even with the most potent poison, one remains at ease. [The monk] asked, "What is it like when neither the person nor the environment are seized?
The Master said, "The village elder knows nothing of the power of Yao and Shun; he beats the drum loudly to sacrifice to the River God. The monk bowed.

Addressing the assembly: When the World-Honored One held up the flower, he was scattering sand before their eyes; when Kāśyapa smiled, his entire body fell into the weeds.
Bodhidharma faced the wall—how bitterly unjust before the Sovereign Heaven! The Second Patriarch sought peace of mind, yet the rat dwelt in gold.
Deshan wielded the staff with reckless abandon; Linji’s shout was like drinking salt to quench thirst. Yangshan’s water-buffalo washed mud in the mire. As for Yangshan...
Plunging in with the spade, one’s very life cannot escape. What principle is there in Juzhi pointing his finger? Xuefeng rolling the ball—old and shameless!

Xuansha not having reached the end—splitting the talk into two pieces. This whole crew of incompetent, frozen old hags were reckless while alive and... dead.
Later, they became coarse and negligent; their offenses filled the heavens and their skulls covered the wilds. Unable to restrain his indignation, I have buried them all in one pit with ignorance.
(He strikes the meditation staff once. It is so that the ten directions of the world are struck with a chilling wind.
Before the Dharma Hall, how could the weeds be merely ten feet deep? You people, tell me: where do you go to vent your breath? Truly!
Jiur said: "When the mind is directed toward it, it is hemmed in by the two Iron Ring Mountains; let it go naturally, and it is pierced through in every direction. He struck once more.
When the guest arrived at the hall, he donned his robes and ascended the Dharma seat. "The Way-master is a great monk," [the guest] thought, "I presumed him to be full of wonders;
yet in truth, he can do nothing. The western wind blows a fine rain, and fallen leaves fill the empty courtyard. A guest comes to visit.
He visited [the mountain], where the green peaks themselves welcomed and saw him off. When the Japanese monk requested the Dharma robes, the Master ascended the hall and cited Shimen Cōng, who said:

The Dharma robe: because people can broaden the Way, it is called the Dharma-body; because there is nowhere it does not pervade and nowhere it does not illuminate, it is called the Dharma-eye.
One Dharma robe from the High Peak Ancestor, I have now this spring requested before the assembly to take to Kōrae (Korea) for offering at Mount Kŭmgang.
One Dharma robe from my late master Huànzhù, I have received and brought here.
"It has been thirty years. Now, the Head Seat Dazhu wishes to invite me back to provide for my needs.

On the fourteenth day of the sixth month of the Dingyou year of the Zheng period, he manifested slight illness. He bathed, changed his robes, assembled the congregation, and spoke this verse:

His secular age was seventy-four and his monastic seniority fifty-six. His disciples used a ceramic niche to enshrine his entire body and interred it at Chongsong Hermitage.
Chan Master Lintu Weize of Shizilin Monastery in Suzhou was a native of Luling in Jixian Prefecture.

His clan name was Tan. He received formal training at Heshan and attained the Dharma under Zhongfeng. A monk asked: "The Buddhas hand over to the Buddhas, and the patriarchs transmit to the patriarchs;

"The Second Patriarch did not go to the Western Heaven, and Bodhidharma did not come to this eastern land; is there still a way for you to benefit others? The Master said, "There is.
[The monk] asked, "What is the Master’s way of benefiting others? The Master said, "In the bathhouse, the lantern laughs until half its mouth is split.
[The monk] said, "Is this not the very place where a student turns themselves around? The Master said, "There is no road to heaven above, and no entrance to the earth below."
The monk said, "Today I am most fortunate to hear the lion’s roar. The Master then gave a shout. The monk bowed.
The Master said, "As for bowing, you may do as you please; however, this one shout has never fallen to the ground.

A monk asked, "The Tathāgata preaches the Dharma with a single voice, yet sentient beings each understand it according to their own kind. I wonder, how does the Master guide people? The Master said, "A frog leaps and hops."
[The monk] said, "Ascending to heaven, the earthworm leaps across the Eastern Sea. The Master asked, "If that is so, then you have transcended the Buddhas and the Patriarchs.

The monk said, "Where do you see this? The Master replied, "From ancient times to the present, it has never fallen; it is clearly right before one's eyes. The Master said, "You are a fabricated Chan practitioner.
A monk from the Huayan Assembly asked, "The boundless realms of all lands are not separated by a hair’s breadth from self and other. Since..."
"How can there be no separation between self and other? The Master said, "The ox in Huai state eats grain; the horse in Yi state has a bloated belly.

"What do you think? The Master said, "In my place, we do not strike; when there is a question, there is an answer.

Addressing the assembly: Zhaozhou spoke of the word "wu" (no). Opening one's mouth reveals the heart and liver.

The Master said, "Do not speak of the dog. Even if you were to ask him whether Śākyamuni and Maitreya possess Buddha-nature, he would also say 'no.

*Wrong!* O Zen adepts, if you can recognize these three points where they were wrong, I will invite you to eat noodles made without flour.

Zen Master Kosen Ingen of Japan’s Kenchō-ji Temple was originally from Sagami Province in his native land. His surname was Fujiwara; the Fujiwara clan was a noble lineage within the nation.

The Master withdrew and wept bitterly, neglecting both food and sleep. Zhongfeng took pity on his sincerity and, because of it...

"To share in life and death with others, and to share in their death, is to naturally accord with the Way.

Even if one were to pour out thousands of Śākyamunis and tens of thousands of Maitreyas, or cause the waters of the four great oceans to enter your faculty of hearing while you remain in a state of non-awakening, it would all be nothing but empty, deluded toil;
none of it would be ultimate. Upon hearing this, the Master was suddenly struck with awe and broke into a cold sweat. One day, having attained realization, he hurried to inform Master Feng.
Yin said, "You have already crashed into the silver mountains and iron walls. Xuefeng asked, "Since you have entered the silver mountains and iron walls, why have you come here?
The Master attained a clear understanding and was relieved. Xuefeng then instructed him, saying, "Protect and maintain this well yourself.
He subsequently studied under the various elders Xu Gu, Ling Gulin, Maodong, Yishai, Yuejiang, and Yin, all of whom called him a "lion cub. At that time—
When the Venerable Seizan Jō returned to his native country, his disciples accompanied him back. He was revered by those both near and far.

One day, manifesting illness, he said to his attendant, "The time has come; bring me a brush and inkstone. He then remarked, "My stupa is already completed, yet its nameplate remains unwritten. Great...
He wrote the two characters "Mind-Seal" (Shixin) and passed away while sitting upright. Initially, his disciples wished to paint a portrait of the Master and requested a eulogy in advance.
The Master drew a perfect circle and inscribed above it: "The wondrous marks are perfectly luminous;
suchness is unmoving. Meeting everywhere, what face is this? His secular age was eighty, and his monastic seniority was sixty-seven.
Chan Master Gumei Zhengyou of Gaoyang Mountain in Jianning Prefecture was a successor of Chan Master Chengyan of Prajñā. He was the son of the Ding family of Guixi.

He received his monastic training under Master Ben of Mount Mo and later studied under Master Juexue, through whom he realized the fundamental tenets of the school. He lived as a wanderer in the Jianghuai region for nearly thirty years.

He longed to find beautiful mountains and waters to build a thatched hut and retire there. Admiring the secluded excellence of Wuyi, he entered Min Province. Initially, he presided over Tianxin in Nanpu.

In the first year of the Taiding era, Jang De-mao, the Magistrate of Jianyang, along with the elder Chen Yi-zong, donated a garden to establish a hermitage and welcomed the Master to open the mountain.
An imperial edict conferred upon him the title "Dajue Miaozhi. Within his quarters, he frequently raised the koan of the "dog has no Buddha-nature."
Regarding the "No Buddha-nature" discourse, the testing with tongs and hammers allows no concessions. At the opening of the retreat, Yangshan ascended the hall:
"The ordinary livelihood of settling the retreat is to emit light from the eyes and draw breath through the nostrils; when hungry, one eats; when weary, one sleeps."

Dust is scattered and sand is tossed in all directions; with a lofty and empty mind, one passes the examination. Entering the hall: Half of the ninety-day period of restraining the feet has already passed.
If the ground of your mind is not yet clear, it is like pulling a fire-drill—do not let your time be spent in vain; resolve this idle koan.
On level ground, without warning, he has caught the thief. This old monk comes forth to deliver a verdict for you. Ascending the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat:
for ninety days of restraining the feet, one has needlessly created error; for three months of summer retreat, one has bound oneself without a rope.
The cloth bag is untied, and heaven and earth are vast and empty. To let go is like seeking tortoise hair; to gather it back is like hanging a hare’s horn. Try hanging both eyes in the void— One.
A cool breeze arises at the corner of the hall. Small Session (Sōsan): The moon sets behind the mountain peaks; clouds span the valley mouth in gloom.

If you wish to clarify the matter of birth and death, you must directly see the person of original nature. Is there anyone here who understands this person of original nature? After a long silence, he said:
When the night is still, there is no need to borrow the moon again; the jade hare always hangs within the great void.

The Master was born in the year of Yiyou of the Zhiyuan era and passed away in the year of Renchen of the Zhizheng era. He preached the Dharma for twenty-nine summers and remained in this world for sixty-eight autumns.

Later, Dongyang, who presided over the monastic center, invited the Master to serve as the Record Keeper. Subsequently, he met Nanchu at Shuangjing.
He shared his seat to preach the Dharma. In the year of Yiwu of the Zheng period, he succeeded to the abbacy at Xifeng Jingtusì.

In the year of Wuxu, the High Emperor personally led the six armies to Wuzhou and visited Zhizhe Temple, issuing an imperial decree appointing the Master as its abbot. In the year of Jiayin, he moved to Jingci Temple.
One day, manifesting a slight illness, he counted on his fingers and said, "It is now the fifth month of summer. His attendants replied, "Indeed. The Master said, "The eighth month."
"The eighth day is most auspicious; I shall depart. When the appointed time arrived, he adjusted his robes, sat upright, and passed away.
His worldly age was sixty-four, and his years as a monk were fifty. He left behind three collections of recorded sermons (*yulu*).
Chan Master Zhizhan Dexiang of Hangzhou was a successor of Chan Master Jingci Lin.
