The Master picked up his whisk and pointed at it, saying, "This was bought for thirty-seven coins. A student asked, "The student has already received a beating before even reaching Qingshan.
The Master said, "You bald-headed meditators! The student said, "I beg you once more to grant me a beating. The Master said, "This old monk has no such leisure energy. The Master’s manner was thus.

His demeanor was dignified and imposing. By nature, he was serene and inclined toward withdrawal from worldly affairs. He attended the Dragon Pond for eighteen years, yet whenever he was repeatedly summoned to share the seat and preach the Dharma, he always declined with humility.
When he first entered Qingu Valley, the snow was so deep that it lasted for over fifty days, during which time the smoke from cooking fires nearly vanished.
The Master remained composed and at ease amidst hungry birds and wild beasts. He thought only of the decline of the Dharma-gate and the late deterioration of his Way.

With great effort, he restored the fundamental principles of the Linji school and extensively expounded the purport of the separate transmission. He bitterly rebuked those who engage in forced interpretation and strictly distinguished between the orthodox and the heterodox.

Scholars from all quarters seeking the Path followed his influence one after another; they vied with one another to fill the land, and Qingshan became renowned during the Yibai year of the Chongzhen era.

On the twenty-third day of the ninth month of the year Guihai, he demonstrated his entry into parinirvāṇa. He was sixty-one years of age and had thirty-seven years of monastic seniority (*bhikṣu-vaṣa*).

His entire body was enshrined in a stūpa at Baoen Monastery. In the Jihai year of the Shunzhi era, his disciples followed his final instructions and relocated the stūpa to the left of Haihui Monastery in Jingxi.
Chan Master Xueqiao Yuanxin of Yunmen in Shaoxing Prefecture was the son of the Zhu family from Ning County.

At the age of nine, he heard the *Amitābha Sūtra* being recited, which stated that "the water birds and the trees all contemplate the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha. Thereupon, he came to know and place his faith in the Buddha Vehicle.
At twenty-nine, he left the household life and later visited Master Zheng at Qinwang. Zheng questioned him regarding the knowledge of others' minds (*paracitta-jñāna*).
"Where have you monks come from? A monk replied, "From India. Xinxin said, "I have heard there are three Indias;
which one have you come from? Speak quickly! Speak quickly! The monk was at a loss for words. Upon hearing this, the Master’s doubt was suddenly aroused.
The following day, he took up his staff, climbed onto a rock, and called out in a loud voice, "Which India have you come from? Speak quickly! Speak quickly! Suddenly—
The past and future limits are severed, like the sun’s disk bursting forth from the midst of space. Then he spoke a verse: “The stone is pressed against the spine;
Turning over, it rests upon the ribs. Look closely at this: Though one moves, one cannot move. He then shouted: “Ha!”
"Zhang San kills a man; Li Si repays him with his life. Desiring to go to Tiantai to seek out a spiritual friend for verification, he suddenly looked up and saw the three characters "Ancient Yunmen.
He attained great enlightenment and spoke a verse, saying: "Once I ascended Tiantai, the clouds grew deeper;
I stepped upon my straw sandals and snapped their cords. The five hundred bhikṣus left no trace; If I were to see them now..."
He broke his tendons and returned to Mount Zhiji (Single Topknot Peak) to live in a thatched hut. He again visited the Great Master Lianchi of Yunqi and presented him with a verse, saying:
"I do not understand the Western Paradise, nor do I study Chan; I have come by chance into this dusty world, simply following conditions.

In a three-room thatched cottage beside a stream I dwell; With two bamboo windows closed, I sleep as the moon passes by. My tattered robes are worn through, so how could there be knots? I let my hair grow long."
Yuchengdian. Since attaining the meaning of the West’s arrival, "White snow falls in the sky of the sixth month.
He subsequently studied under Longchi, with whom he attained karmic resonance within the meditation hall. In the forty-third year of the Wanli era, he moved to Qianzhi-an at Mount Jing.
Later, he resided at Kaixian on Mount Lu. In the Guiwei year, he moved to Dongta in Jiahe. In his later years, he stayed at Yunmen in Yue. A monk asked: "How is it?"
"This is the tradition of the Shuangji family," the Master said. "A single mound of earth for a stove atop ten thousand peaks. A monk asked, "Whose Dharma heir is the Great Master?
The Master said, "From afar, one watches all day as the iron ox bellows within the clouds. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "To break two into three. The monk asked, "What is the intent behind this? The Master said, "It is what is commonly called 'the mundane.'"

[The Master] spoke. A monk asked, "When the moon rises above the horizon, how is it? The Master said, "What kind of season is that? [The monk] asked, "When the trees wither and the leaves fall, how is it?
The Master said, "The birds do not roost. A monk asked, "When the four elements disperse, where does one go?
The Master said, "Into the coffin. [The monk] asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "Buried in the earth. The monk bowed, and the Master then...
[He] shouted and ascended the hall. "For forty years I have practiced in this way; I have slashed open the azure sky until it reeks with blood. Within it lies a truly wondrous matter:

the lion roams without asking for directions. He prostrated to the Tathāgata King of Lamps and universally vowed that the sentient beings of lands as numerous as motes of dust would all enter the gate of Prajñāpāramitā. "Great assembly, tell me: what is Prajñā?"
"How does one enter the gate of the *pāramitās*? [The Master] raised his whisk and said, "To discern. He then ascended the seat and said:

"To see that the body has no reality is the Buddha-body; to realize that the mind is like an illusion is the Buddha-illusion. To realize that the nature of both body and mind is empty—how can such a person differ from the Buddha?
Master Mo said, "I, the Senior Monk, do not think so. The eel gathers at the bottom of the water; the hawk flies close to the sky. Understand!"

If you grasp the meaning within this, there will be no further doubt regarding the attainment of Buddhahood. In the eighth year of the Chongzhen era, the Protector of the Dharma Yu Dacheng, Governor of the Province, along with Huang Duanduo, the Judicial Commissioner, and others visited the Master and requested him to ascend the Dharma Hall for a formal discourse at the Great Hall of Jing Mountain. "Du! Du! Du! (Thump! Thump! Thump!)
This is the Jingshan of the Tang and Song dynasties. [The Master] strikes the whisk. Eighty-one people have passed through here;
this is not the Jingshan of today, nor is it the Jingshan of a single day. For a thousand years the monastery has remained, yet for a single morning there is but one monk.
Today the Patriarchal Command is being put into action, cutting off all ten directions. Tell me, is there any auspicious sign? [He rings] the bell.
"The bell tower has grown ears; the Buddha Hall is also pregnant. Huang Gong asked, "What is meant by 'the bell tower has grown ears'?
The Master picked up the incense burner and said, "Understand this! Huang asked, "What is meant by 'the Buddha Hall is also pregnant'? The Master said, "It has given birth.
Huang bowed and said, "Truly, it must be the Master who can do this. The Master then said, "Now, on behalf of the assembly..."
The donor has invited this old monk to ascend this seat to restore the desolate ancestral hall and uphold the collapsing traditions of the past.
This is what is called "a dog's tail following a fox's fur. Who cares about the torches burning before every door?
I shall not ask about "Xie Sanlang on the fishing boat," but rather: "The daughter-in-law rides the donkey while the mother-in-law leads it"—speak a single phrase!
"Is there anyone who can speak of this? With one sweep of the whisk, the moon in the golden palace is struck open; among the ten thousand households, there is none that is not illuminated.
On that day, several lay practitioners invited the Master for a meal at the Han Cui Lou.

The Master said, "This old monk is sixty-six years old this year," and he again counted his fingers, saying, "Bing, Ding, Wu, Ji, Geng. After a long while, he remarked, "I am surprised that people keep pulling me back and forth."
It turns out that the Water Buffalo has entered the palace of life; it drags through the mud and carries water, touching the east and touching the west.

Nevertheless, one may rejoice that there is plenty of water and plenty of grass. One day, he manifested a slight illness and wrote a verse of parting for the assembly, saying: "Little children! On the road of birth and death, you must be carefree.
When the moon is bright and the frost is clear at dawn, drink a cup of tea and depart while sitting. Having finished writing, he threw down his brush.
He passed away on the twenty-sixth day of the eighth month of the Dinghai year. His worldly age was seventy-seven and his monastic seniority forty-eight.
His entire body was enshrined in a stupa at the right foot of Mount Yunmen.
Chan Master Dalian Jingming Baopu of Huzhou was the son of the Luo family of Lin’an. At the age of fifteen, he went to Miaoyan to receive the tonsure;
at twenty-two, he went to Yunqi to receive full ordination. Initially, he frequented lecture halls. One day, he thought to himself:
"For several years now, although I have reached a point of understanding regarding the principles of the scriptural teachings, they are of no use whatsoever at the brink of birth and death."
He then changed his clothes and entered Mount Jing. During the thirty-seven-day period of intensive meditation, he attained a state of vast, transparent penetration.
He composed a verse, saying: "Since childhood I lost my mother; I searched for her everywhere in foreign lands. Suddenly, we met face to face— No further deliberation was needed."
Upon concluding the retreat, he went directly to Jingxi to visit Master Hanyou at Longchi. He asked, "I have come from afar to seek the wind of your teaching;
I beg the Master for instruction. Longchi said, "This old monk’s teeth are sparse and missing. The Master replied, "Please grant me one word regarding the most intimate point."
Daci took his seat. The Master called for an attendant to bring some tea. Daci said, "The Senior Monk is quite clever.
The Master said, "I am deaf. Daci then desisted. One day, as the Master was taking his leave, Daci said, "I, this old monk, still have words that remain unsaid.
The Master said, "Though the Master’s words are not yet finished, I already know their meaning. Daci said, "Then tell me—"
"What is the old monk’s intention? The Master then gave a shout. Chengchi said, "Try giving another shout and see. The Master turned around and went out.
Chengchi then bestowed upon him the lineage whisk. Later, while staying there, a monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'Buddha'? The Master said, "The meaning of awakening.
The monk asked, "Is a Buddha still deluded? The Master said, "Yes, he is deluded. The monk asked, "If he has already awakened, why does he become deluded again? The Master said:

Not being deluded, he asked again, "What is it? The monk said, "One must still ask for clarification. The Master raised his staff and struck him out. He asked, "What is 'seizing the person but not seizing the environment'?
The Master said, "A swallowtail butterfly pierces through the flowers. He asked, "What is 'seizing the environment but not seizing the person'?
The Master said, "Lifting the eyebrows, one sweeps away the white clouds. He asked, "What is 'seizing both person and environment'? The Master said:
There was no news from either side. [A monk] asked, "What is it like when both person and environment are not wrested away? The Master said, "Push open the window and look at the bright moon.
The layman Xiong of Yushan asked, "All dharmas return to the One; to what does the One return? The Master raised his tea cup and said, "Please have some tea.
Xiong said, "I made a cotton shirt in Qingzhou that weighed seven pounds—what do you say to that? The Master...
He said, "A turtle shedding its shell flies up into the sky. When asked, "What is the meaning of 'three catties of hemp'? the Master replied, "The weight is clearly distinguished.
The Master entered nirvana on the eighth day of the eighth month in the second year of the Chongzhen era.

Chan Master Yuanhu Miaoyong of Puming Monastery in Jiaxing Prefecture was a successor of Chan Master Xingshan Guang. He was the son of Zheng of Haining and received his monastic training under Master Nanyue Mingguang of Xingshan.
He once visited Master Wuhuan Chong to receive instruction on the essentials of the Dharma. Later, while spending the summer retreat at Mount Jing, he happened upon—
Upon reading the *Suyī jīng* (Sūtra of Further Increase), he attained a realization. He composed a verse and presented it to Guǎng, who rebuked him. He served [Guǎng] for several years.
One day, while examining the *Chuándēng lù*, he reached the case concerning Master Yǎn’s descendant, Gōngān Qīngfēng; his mental blockages were suddenly cleared away.
Later, while conversing with Grand Master Xuěqiáo during the night, Xuě suddenly pointed at the moon and said, "That half-moon—where has it gone? The Master was then profoundly enlightened.
After a long silence, Xue said, "I have only obtained half of it. The Master asked, "Where has that other half gone? Xue remained silent for another long while.
The Master said, "I too have only obtained half of it. One day, he prepared to pass away. He requested a brush and wrote a verse:
"Life is a mistake; death is a mistake. The iron ox snaps the golden rope. He threw down the brush and said, "Tut! Then he passed away peacefully.
This was the eleventh day of the tenth month in the fifteenth year of the Chongzhen era.

Chan Master Yinzhu of Puan at Cihua in Yuanzhou (the seventeenth generation under Dajian):
A native of the Yu clan from Yichun in this same prefecture. His mother was surnamed Huang.
He was born on the twenty-seventh day of the eleventh month in the year of Yiwei of the Zhenghe era. At the time of his birth, there were extraordinary signs. At the age of fifteen, he went to...
He received his training from Master Shoulong Xian. Xian transmitted the *Lotus Sūtra* to him, but the Master said, "The profound purport of all Buddhas values awakening to one's own mind;
what benefit does counting characters and following the lines of the text provide for the Way? Xian was greatly amazed by this and had him serve diligently at his side.
After seven years, he finally received the tonsure and the full precepts. He then went to Mount Wei to visit Mukan.

Upon rising from his prostrations, the Master asked, "All phenomena return to the One; where does the One return? Mukan raised his whisk and showed it to him. At that moment, the Master attained realization of the fundamental meaning.
He soon returned to his studies for more than ten years. Upon reaching the *guīyǒu* year of the Shaoxing era, he finally accepted the invitation from Cihu.

After he took up residence, both monastics and laypeople unanimously turned toward his influence; all necessary conditions converged, and within a few years, the Buddhist temple was adorned with gold and azure tiles as if descended from heaven.

Its grandeur and exquisite beauty were preeminent in the region south of the Lake. Although the Master had appeared through the power of his vows to save beings and benefit all life, he still felt that what he had attained was not yet sufficient.

For twelve years, he remained diligent day and night, his side never touching the mat. One day, while reading the *Huayan He lun* (Compendium on the Avataṃsaka), he reached the passage where "the mind's nature is forgotten and the essence of the mind is realized as one.
At that moment, he experienced a sudden and great awakening. He then composed [this verse]:
The verse says: "It cannot be squeezed into a ball, nor can it be pulled apart; why seek further at Nanyue or Tiantai? At the gateway of the six sense-faculties, no one makes use of it;

this has provoked a foreign monk to come here for no reason. Later, on the twenty-first day of the seventh month in the Jichou year of the Qiandao era (1169), he suddenly requested a brush and wrote a verse on the western wall of his chamber.
He then bathed, changed his robes, sat in the lotus position, and passed away. His age was... [text ends].
He lived to the age of fifty-five and had twenty-eight years of monastic seniority (*saṃgha-rakṣā*). His entire remains were enshrined in a stupa at his native mountain.
Four volumes of his recorded sayings (*yù-lù*) circulate in the world. He was a Dharma successor of Chan Master Yuehuan (under the lineage of Da Jian, the twenty-seventh generation).
Chan Master Wunian Yuanxin of Funiu was the son of the Gao family from Jintai.
He was born in the Jiyou year of the Xuande era. At the age of nine, he left home to become a monk; after receiving full ordination, he first visited Wuji at Long’en, where he attained realization.

In the Jimao year of the Tianshun era, he returned to Mount Niu to build a thatched hut. In the Xinsi year, he again traveled to Fanchang to visit Yuehuan. Yuehuan asked him, “From where have you come?”
[The Master] said, "Niu Mountain. Huan said, "People are here; where is the ox? The Master said, "Face-to-face, yet we do not recognize each other;
its entire body is revealed, vast and majestic. Huan said, "Even so, its horns and head are not fully present. The Master said, "I am weary from walking the mountain today.
Huan again picked up his bamboo staff and said, "If you call it a bamboo staff, it is a 'stirring' [obstacle]; if you do not call it..."
[Zhaozhou] made a bamboo whisk and showed it to the Abbot [Fanhui], saying, "What do you say to this? The Master said, "It is a waste of mental effort. Fanhui said, "Not yet; speak further.
The Master then stepped forward, snatched the whisk away, and threw it to the ground. Fanhui laughed heartily. The Master said, "I have committed an offense," and he prostrated himself.
Fanhui then patted him and certified his realization. The Master lived in seclusion in a hermitage for thirty years before opening the Dharma.
Funiu. A monk asked, "Pang Jushi said, 'There is but one kind of stringless lute;
only you, Master, can play it wondrously. Today I beg the Master to play it for me. The Master coughed once. The monk said, "I do not understand.
The Master said, "The bell rings as a bell; the drum sounds as a drum. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "Mazu has been gone for a long time."
The questioner asked, "What is 'this very mind is Buddha'? The Master said, "A wealthy man is easily arrogant. The questioner asked, "And what about 'neither mind nor Buddha'?
The Master said, "A deep pit is difficult to fill. The questioner said, "I do not understand.
The Master said, "To say 'this very mind is Buddha' is much like gouging a sore into healthy flesh; to say 'neither mind nor Buddha' is no different from applying moxa to a sore."
Even if you say it is not mind, not Buddha, and not an object, you will still stumble on level ground. But tell me, how is it ultimately?
Sitting down, he wipes the table and adds incense; after the gruel is finished, he calls the boy to wash the bowls.
Chan Master Zhengfa Xueguang of Qianzhong (28th generation under Dajian), whose secular surname was Zhao, was a dharma heir of Chan Master Jiekong Tong.

Having traveled extensively throughout various regions, he spent the summer retreat at Lingfeng, where upon hearing the case of Venerable Yan’yang’s question to Master Zhaozhou, he attained realization. He presented his understanding to Jizhao, who said, “There is none.”

This is precisely the point where you must apply your effort; do not mistake a mere fragment of light and shadow, lest it mislead your entire life. He again entered the winter retreat at Jingde Temple.

One day, while in meditative concentration, he was triggered by the sound of a mountain waterfall. He silently brought to mind the kōans of the patriarchs and Buddhas of the past and penetrated them one by one.
He then went to visit Jiekong and recounted his realizations from the beginning. Jiekong said: "Have you not heard it said?"
"Do not say that 'no-mind' is the Way; no-mind still leaves behind a further barrier. Upon hearing this, the Master immediately entered his chamber.

From then on, he was bewildered and lost in thought, harboring doubts and unable to reach a decision. One day, seeing the line from a poem by Hanshan, "My mind is like the autumn moon," his lingering obstructions were suddenly released.
Later, he lived in a hermitage on Mount Gu, where he passed away after writing a verse at the time of his death.
The Chan Master Xuefeng Rui (28th generation below Dajian), the Venerable Xingkong, once composed the "Song of Manifesting the School" (*Xianzong ge*), which says:
To realize this school, there is neither past nor present; One breaks through empty space and then mends it oneself.
Amidst a mass of sounds and forms lies the field of wondrous enlightenment; In letting go and gathering back, there is no obstruction. The wondrousness within the essence—
At midnight, a wooden man stands before a mirror; on the southern shore of Persia, one chews cold ice. In the northern borderlands, the barbarian children bustle through the market streets.
Within the midst of utility lies the profound mystery: a stone woman blows a flute atop a verdant tree; a gourd from Zhaozhou hangs upon the eastern wall;

in the village, the old Wang burns paper money at night. This is the mystery within mystery, the wondrous within wonder: amidst a lattice of precious silk, bright pearls compete for brilliance. One must turn toward...
A single aperture pierces the darkness; the ocean-tide voice speaks with blazing intensity. A lute of lion-sinew plays the "White Snow" melody;
the green mountains on both banks smile and nod their heads. After a hundred years, the forms of foxes and hares are crushed and extinguished.
The Dharma Heir of Chan Master Dachantong (the twenty-ninth generation under Dajian):
The Venerable Junfeng Qingxiang had long relied upon Dachantong. One day, he suddenly attained realization and presented this verse:
"The Dharma-nature is empty and unimpeded; In its equality, it is Avalokiteśvara. Severing the dualistic workings of mind, This is called transcending the three realms."

Chan Master Lanmu Zhanjue of Yuan Tong Monastery in Jingzhou (the twenty-ninth generation under Dajian), a dharma heir of National Teacher Xingkong, was born into the Zhang family of Qujiang in Chang’an. From his youth, he aspired to the joy of Chan;
he received the tonsure under Master Xiuan at Lantian and resolved to investigate and clarify the great matter of birth and death, persevering day and night.

He applied himself with such diligence that he neglected both sleep and food. One day, he attained a realization and went to see Xingkong to seek his definitive resolution; he was subsequently granted certification.
In the *Bingxu* year of the Chenghua era, he opened the Dharma at Yuan Tong. Entering the hall, he said: "In this field where Buddhas are selected, the weeds grow three feet deep."
In the Hall of the Empty King, waves surge a thousand fathoms high. The Perfect Penetration has a single phrase that cannot be disgorged whole;
if it is disgorged, it is no longer whole. If there is anyone who can examine this through and through, I grant them the possession of one eye.

Compiled by the Ancestral Successor, Śramaṇa Tōng-wèn of Eastern Wu;
Collected by the Layman of Li-zé, Shī Pèi of Huátíng. Ming Dynasty.
Dharma Heir of Chan Master Jingci Hui of the Sixteenth Generation under Dajian of the Cao-Dong School.
Chan Master Mingji Huizu of Huazang Monastery in Changzhou cited the koan of Dongshan eating fruit on a winter night.
His verse says: Who does not have their share of Dongshan’s fruit? He withdrew the tray—a wondrous turning of the pivot.
Tonight I shall lightly reveal it for you: A sleeping cat beneath a peony flower.
Chan Master Weigan Daqin of Guangfu Temple in Taizhou, a dharma heir of Chan Master Xuedou Chong, was the son of the Yu family of that prefecture. He ascended the hall and said:
"A monk asked Tong’an, 'What is the house style of the Master? An replied: 'The golden rooster carries its chick back to the void; the jade hare..."
[The Master] was pregnant when he entered the Ziwai [Palace]. [Someone] asked, "If a guest suddenly arrives, how will you receive them?
An said, "The golden fruit was plucked by the monkey at early court; the jade flower is carried back by the phoenix after evening. The Teacher said, "Guangfu would not do so.
If someone asks, 'What is the house style of the Master? I would simply say to him: 'Beside the grove of green bamboos, one sings the *kuan-nai*; deep within the blue cliffs..."*
Reclining amidst the misty vines, suddenly encountering a guest—how shall one receive them? A bottomless basket holds the bright moon;
a mindless bowl stores the pure breeze.

On the occasion of opening the furnace, Chan Master Zao of Chao-hua in Yuezhou, successor to Chan Master Shanquan Zhi, ascended the hall and said: "Snow fills the cold window; the wooden Buddha of Danxia has been burned away.
Ice freezes the wild crossing; the iron ox of Shanzhou has been frozen to death. It reaches the point where cold ashes emit flames, yet not a single flake of snow remains."

Remain. Spontaneously and freely, it manifests as the enjoyment of reality. Do all you practitioners of Chan understand? Wrapping one’s head in a patched robe, sitting there, one has no awareness at all of heat or cold.

Chan Master Zuanan Zhijian of Xuedou in Mingzhou was a dharma successor of Chan Master Tiantong Ju. He was the son of the Wu family of Chuzhou. When he was a child, his mother was washing his hands and sores;
he asked her, "What is this? The Master replied, "How does my hand compare to the Buddha-hand? His parents passed away when he was young.
Zhenxie relied upon Changlu; at that time, Dayu was in the position of the First Seat and held him in high esteem. Later, Zhenxie lived in seclusion at Mount Xiangshan.
One night, he attained awakening and sought verification from Yanshou. He then returned to see Dayu. While presiding over the assembly in the Dharma Hall, Dayu said:
"The World-Honored One has a secret word; Kāśyapa did not conceal it. One night, a rain of falling blossoms; the flowing water in the stream is full of fragrance."
The Dharma heir of the seventeenth generation under Great Mirror (Dajian Huineng), Chan Master Donggu Guang of Huazang, ascended the hall and said:
"In the place where the body hides, there is no trace; atop the shadowless tree dwells the numinous bird."
Where there are no traces, do not hide yourself; on the sproutless branch, spring blossoms burst open. There is a source from which they come—who can discern it?
At daybreak, the west wind sweeps softly; along a single path, pine needles are scattered and cast about.
Chan Master Chang’ung Ru Jing of Tiantong in Mingzhou was a dharma successor of Chan Master Xuedou Jian. From birth, he was exceptionally precocious and unlike ordinary children.

As he grew up, he studied the world-transcending Dharma and went to Xuedou to study under Zu’an. While contemplating the koan of the "Cypress Tree in the Courtyard," he attained realization and presented a verse:
He said: "The ancestral meaning from the West is the cypress tree in front of the courtyard; nostrils vast and empty, facing the eyes.

A withered branch falling to the ground, just as it leaps and bounds, the pine and the creeper laugh aloud in exuberance. Yan'an approved of this. He spent several decades in the world [of teaching], later moving to Jingci Temple, and subsequently received an imperial decree to ascend to Tiantong.
Holding up the imperial edict, he showed it to the assembly, saying: "The clouds part, and the nine heavens reveal the rising sun."

Behold the variegated phoenix bringing it forth. But tell me, how can you truly comprehend this? *Ji-ji ru lü-ling* (Urgent as the Imperial Decree). The Imperial Decree: Opening the Furnace, Ascending the Hall.
He summons the assembly and draws a perfect circle, saying: "This is the Tiantong furnace. Approach it and you will be burned to death; retreat and you will freeze to death.
Suppose a man were to come forward and ask, 'What should be done?'—the moment he speaks, the furnace moves! *Shang* (Ascending).
In the Hall: The frosty wind howls with a chilling severity; the frost-touched leaves fall in a whistling tumult.
Raising his whisk, he said: "Look! Only the Linglong Cliff towers ever higher. This so-called "stale ware" of Tiantong is put on sale today for a single short-term auction.

Is there anyone who can offer a price? [He] descended from the seat. Ascending the hall to tour the quarters: Neither allowing entry from without nor exit from within—strike it down with a painful blow!
The mallet! All matters are now concluded. But tell me, how so? Before the Peak of Great White, the mandate is renewed; both internal and external regulations are fully established.
Entering and exiting the two orders, he ascends the hall: he opens the Avīci Hell and manifests King Yama.
He assembles a host of yakṣas and arranges the ox-head demons in two rows. For those who advance, the fierce flames upon the sword-trees are employed.
Rather than retreating to the mountain of blades or the cold ice for concealment, one should first comprehend the principle of things.

It is unbearable to fiddle with chopsticks when full of food, or to pass stool and urinate upon the bed when pressed by nature. If this is not yet so, then the willows and flowers of spring enter the theater.
Ascending the hall: Tian Tong’s iron-smelling old fisthead has slaughtered the water-buffalo of the rivers and lakes.
At nightfall, suddenly an egg is born; at daybreak, the great sun is pushed forth. Tell me, how does it dry the places where all of you are soaked?

Startled by this, he went with him to Seon’ak to visit Master Hyu-rim, the Ancient Buddha, saying, "This child is of the lineage of a dragon-elephant (nāga).
If he may attend upon you as your attendant, he will surely become a great vessel in the future. Hyu-rim accepted him, shaved his head, and conferred the full precepts (*upasampadā*) upon him.

He served alongside Ssang-hye for seven years. At that time, Wansong was residing at Bogeum-sa; the Master would often pack his belongings in a cloth bag and go there alone to enter the master’s quarters.

His inner capacity was in accord with the Dharma, and he subsequently received the master’s seal of approval (*kṣānti*). He remained in close attendance for several years before later residing at Shaoshi.

When the future Emperor Shizu was still in his private residence, he commanded the Master to preside over a Great *Pratimokṣa* Precept Assembly. In the year Wushen, an imperial edict summoned him to reside at Xingguo Monastery in Helin.

Following Shizu’s accession to the throne, a debate arose concerning apocryphal scriptures; the Master dispatched an express courier to report this to the court. The false texts were burned, and the Master was bestowed the title "Guangzong Zhengbian" (Orthodox Discernment of the Radiant Ancestor) and commanded [to remain].
He immediately built a vihāra in his native village and was granted the imperial edict naming it "Bao'en" (Requiting Kindness). He was further granted fields to provide food for the assembly.
At that time, the seat at Wanshou Monastery was vacant, and the community again requested the Master to preside over it. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "Wait until Milk Peak nods its head, and I shall tell you. Another asked, "What is the singular path of the Honored and Noble? The Master said, "The fisherman..."
The song startles the herons on the sandy islets; they fly out from the reeds, their traces unseen. The Master asked a monk, "The Way-source is not far, and the ocean of nature is not distant;
tell me, where does it reside? The monk hesitated, and the Master gave a shout. In his later years, he retired to live at Songyang.
On the twentieth day of the seventh month of the year Yihai, he manifested a slight illness, gathered the assembly, wrote a verse, and passed away. His worldly age was...
He had seventy-three years of monastic seniority (sang-lak) and was fifty-two [years of age]. His stupa was erected in the western corner of his residence.
He was the twenty-fifth generation descendant of Dajian (Mahākāśyapa) and a dharma heir of Chan Master Shaoshi.

Master Wentai of Lingyin on Mount Shaoshi in the Western Capital was exceptionally brilliant and insightful from his youth. Having studied under Xueting, he attained a profound and intuitive realization of the profound essence of the teachings.
Later, he succeeded him as the abbot. Upon ascending the hall for a formal discourse, he said: "The events of kalpas past and future exist only in this very moment."
The wondrous virtues as numerous as the sands of the Ganges are all within the source of the mind. Try having him present them directly, face-to-face;

yet he does not know how to bring them forth against the wind. Tell me, where does the fault lie? He strikes the staff and says: "It is precisely because it is so utterly clear that what is attained is delayed."
Chan Master Zhitaï of Zhonglin at Ba’en Temple in Taoyuan Prefecture was a native of Yucheng in Fenyang. His clan name was Wen.
Having shaved his head and beard in the Huayan tradition, he one day sighed with deep emotion, saying, "A man of great character should investigate and clarify the great matter of birth and death;
how can one confine oneself to such trivialities? He then went to visit Xueting at Wanshou Temple, where he served him diligently for several years.

His spiritual resonance was harmonized within the inner quarters of his master’s room. Later, by imperial decree, he resided at Baoen Monastery. One day, manifesting illness, he gathered the assembly and said, "My karmic conditions have ended here.
You all must protect and uphold yourselves well; cherish every moment and do not let it pass in vain.
He then wrote a verse: "The Master Xi Qi has built a seamless stupa; I have toppled my own formless body. The formless body—formless."
His body was the formless body, within which all traces of dust were extinguished. Having finished writing, he passed away with a serene expression.
Chan Master Jingxu of Zu’an at Lingyan in Taian Prefecture was the son of the Zhang family of Yongping.

He received his formal training at Shousheng Monastery on Mount Xiangshan and traveled to various regions for over twenty years, meeting several spiritual teachers, yet found none with whom he reached accord. Later, he visited Xue...

He served at Wanshou for a long time, where he received personal instruction and attained certification of his realization. He first resided at Wanshou, then moved to Shaoshi and Lingyan, and later retired to Xiangshan.
One day, he gathered the assembly to bid them farewell and passed away lying on his right side. (Chan Master Zhonglin composed an inscription for him, which says:)

The nostrils reach the vast heavens; the heels touch the ground. With a clear mind and upright eyes, his conduct is ancient and his countenance warm. As his deeds grow greater, his resolve becomes more steadfast. Elders from all quarters knock at his door; he is the dharma-heir of Xueting and the grandson of Wansong.

His wheel of activity turns with the speed of lightning and the roar of thunder. He plants the banner high upon the tree of enlightenment and firmly consolidates the spiritual roots. His lamp of wisdom shines brightly, melting away the masses of darkness. With his total capacity and great function, he shakes heaven and overturns earth. He tosses over the Bohai Sea and kicks down Mount Kunlun. He swallows the Buddhas of the three periods of time in a single gulp.

Unstuck by the two extremes, what need is there to discuss the Middle Way? Residing in great monasteries for three terms, he is revered by the fourfold assembly. Coming and going, there is no trace; moving or still, there is no mark. Though empty space may crumble, this Way remains forever.
The twenty-sixth generation descendant of Dajian, Chan Master Tai of Shaoshi, had as his dharma heir Chan Master Huan-yuan Fuyu of Baoying in the Western Capital.
He was a native of the Wang family of Lingshi in Huozhou. He relied upon [the monastery] in that district...
At Tuṣita Monastery, he cut through all defilements and traveled extensively among lecture halls, where he was renowned as the "Tiger of Meaning.
Later, he departed to pay his respects at Lingyin, where he devoted himself with sincerity and entered the Master’s room. One day, hearing Lingyin ascend the hall and cite: "Do not seek from others;

to do so is to distance yourself from me," the Master suddenly attained liberation. He was immediately granted certification. Subsequently, he resided at Tianqing and later moved to Baoying. A monk asked: "What is the Patriarch?"

This is the general meaning of the transmission from the West. The Master said: "The wind carries the sound of the spring to the side of my pillow; the moon shifts the shadows of the flowers onto the window.
He passed away in the tenth month of the Gui-chou year of the Huangqing era. His worldly age was sixty-nine, and his years as a monk were forty-nine.
Chan Master Qiu Jiangjie of Lingyan in Jinan Prefecture went to visit Xue Xuan. The Master asked, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Qingzhou.
The Master said, "Did you bring the Qingzhou cloth robe with you? He replied, "I have already presented it to the Master. The Master accepted him and directed him to attend the hall.
After a long time, one day he suddenly attained great enlightenment. He then went to the abbot’s quarters; before he had even opened his mouth—
The Master suddenly said, "The golden lock of the mysterious pass has been opened. Xuan replied, "What kind of old kernel do you seek within a peach pit that is a thousand years old?
The Master then instructed him, saying, "This is something you have possessed from the beginning. Guard and maintain it well.
In days to come, who other than you could propagate my Way?"

Chan Master Yueyan Yongda of Baoying Temple in the Western Capital was a dharma successor of Chan Master Lingyan Su. He was a native of the Liu clan of Fenzhou and received his monastic training at Tianning Temple in his hometown.

Constantly using the reality of birth and death as a catalyst for spiritual urgency, he went to visit Lingyan, who held him in high esteem. After several years of personal attendance and study under him...
He then entered the innermost chamber and said, "Realization arises from the teacher, but its practice depends on oneself.

He subsequently went to Tàishān to close his retreat, but at the request of the fourfold assembly, he was compelled to reside at Bǎoyìng. Later, manifesting a slight illness, he sat upright and passed away.
Chan Master Fulong Guyan Pujiu was a native of Huyang. His clan name was Liu. At the age of fifteen, he left the household life at Chanqing Temple.

He first visited Lingyan, who instructed him with the hammer and tongs of the fundamental school. Before long, he attained awakening. In the sixth year of the Dade era, Yue’an Hai retired from his position;
the various mountain monasteries submitted a formal petition requesting the Master to fill the vacancy. By imperial decree, he was bestowed the title Miaoyan Hong.
The Dharma Master Fada’s title was [bestowed]. He subsequently moved his residence to Longfeng and later retired to Lingqi. He passed away at the age of seventy-seven.
He belonged to the twenty-seventh generation under Dajian (Huineng).

Chan Master Xiangyan Chunzhu Wencai of Dengzhou was a dharma successor of Chan Master Baoying Yu. He was the son of the Yao family in Linfen, Pingyang Prefecture. From birth he possessed extraordinary qualities;
whenever he saw a monk, he would join his palms and pay homage. Upon reaching a slight age, he went to follow Master Fuyan Pu to receive instruction. Once, he...
While reading the *Song of Realizing the Way*, he reached the line, "The illusory, transformed, empty body is itself the Dharma-body," and joyfully attained realization.
He then went to visit Huairan to present his understanding; Huairan certified his attainment. Subsequently, he spent three years reading the Tripitaka at Longmen.
In the Jiazi year of the Taiding era, he presided over Shaoshi, and later moved to Xiangyan. When a monk asked, "What is the realm of principle? the Master replied, "Empty space."
It fell to the ground and shattered into fragments, leaving no trace. [The student] asked, "What is the dharma-realm of phenomena?

The Master said, "Having arrived, the house is utterly emptied; one need not be a fool within the dwelling. [The student] asked, "What is the dharma-realm of the non-obstruction between principle and phenomena?

The Master said, "In the depths of winter, the withered tree flourishes; in the height of summer, the snow-flower falls. [The student] asked, "What is the dharma-realm of the non-obstruction between all phenomena? The Master—

He said, "The clear breeze accompanies the bright moon; the rustic old man smiles as we draw near. On the seventeenth day of the fifth month of the *Renchen* year of the *Zhizheng* era, he bathed, changed his robes, assembled the congregation, and issued a final admonition.
At dawn the following day, he passed away in auspicious tranquility. His entire body was interred to the right of the Xueting Stupa.
He was eighty years of age at the time of his death.
Chan Master Xuexuan Daocheng of Tianjie Monastery in Jinling was a dharma heir of Chan Master Lingyan Jie. He was a distant descendant of the Great King Zhao of Yunzhou;
his father moved to Baoding, where they subsequently settled. At the age of fifteen, the Master received the tonsure at Xingguo Temple in the prefecture. He had a broad forehead.

He possessed a flat crown and a majestic, imposing bearing. From an early age, he harbored great aspirations; as soon as he had received full ordination, he joined a group of companions to secretly investigate the principles of the Single Transmission.
Later, hearing of the flourishing reputation of Master Qiujiang’s Dharma seat, he went there to seek instruction (the details of which are recorded in Lingyan Jie’s chapter).

He soon returned to Qingshe, where both monastics and laypeople requested that he take up residence at Puzhao Monastery. In the fifteenth year of the Hongwu era, an imperial edict established the Sangha Administration, and the Master was selected for office.

In the eighth month of the autumn of the thirtieth year, an imperial edict commanded the Master to take up residence at Tianjie Monastery. The Master submitted a memorial stating that he did not understand the Buddha-dharma.

The Emperor composed a poem in his own hand and bestowed it upon him, saying: "He declined my words and consented to remain silent; He returned westward with his single shoe, following the ancient direct transmission.

At the Hall of the Empty King, on the first and fifteenth days, The drums and bells resound as he takes his seat from years past. Ascending the hall, he said: "Ten thousand acres of white clouds roll away..."
The true mechanism beyond the kalpas of *śūralu* is revealed; the crimson leaves upon a thousand peaks brilliantly manifest this wondrous principle within.

It has never been obscured throughout antiquity and remains forever enduring across dust-like kalpas. The bird-path is empty yet penetrating; the movement of steps through the dark portal is subtle and dense.

The lion’s strings fall in rhythmic succession, and as the fingers press them, ancient tones ring out with resonance. This reaches the point where the stone woman nods her head and the wooden man claps his hands. Grasp it!
Raising the golden needle and threading the jade line, one passes through the vanguard of the mechanism. Cutting off the hare’s horns and tortoise hair, one illuminates that which is above.

The orthodox and the deviant are revealed alone; the hidden and the manifest are fully encompassed. Therefore, in every thing, at every head, in every speck of dust and every moment of space, there is not even a hair’s breadth lacking.
Do you all understand? Last night a wooden horse passed through the clouds, startling the Southern Dipper and the Northern Dipper.
Douzang ascended the hall and said: "When yin reaches its limit, yang returns and the days grow longer; plum blossoms everywhere emit their fragrant scent.
Within this, there is not much of a secret to be told—how could it ever be hidden throughout the entire world? Thus, with such clarity and transparency, we meet at the tips of the hundred grasses;
with such dense and profound proclamation, it is uniquely revealed within the light of the ten thousand phenomena. Realize it upon the field of profit and fame."
The True Person of No Rank reveals his original face amidst the mountains of self and others. His shadow encompasses the mirror of the school. When the mind arises, all manner of phenomena arise;
the body is the site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*). When the mind ceases, all manner of phenomena cease.

The barren woman holds high the precious seal, its patterns fully manifest; the wooden man silently passes through the golden shuttle, not missing even a hair’s breadth. He pulls and moves that which lies beyond the kalpas.
The pivot of the mechanism: blazing like the sun and moon within the world, it secretly penetrates both near and far. It is such that even withered wood can bloom with flowers;
it encompasses all things from antiquity to the present, capable of causing ice-cold frost to emit flames. Clouds shroud the ancient path where the lingering colors of the wilds remain lost;

the moon fills the cold crags as a brilliant divine light shines everywhere. When the mechanisms of the six gates are stilled, there is no need for circuitous detours or indirect references—it is but a single color.
The work is complete. One must strictly avoid being struck at the head and broken. The white ox treading its path has already received the conditions for transformation and edification;

the jade horse neighing in the wind is entirely a matter of benefiting sentient beings. But tell me, what is the matter that transcends this? *Pah!* A staff of rabbit horns picks up the moon from the bottom of the pond;
a whisk of tortoise hair hangs upon the clouds over the mountain peaks. [Ascending the hall: When the three yang lines intersect in harmony, all things flourish.
New! It reveals the wondrous function of the single truth and embodies the profound source of all transformation. In every atom one merges with the Way; in every place there is a passage.

The Dharma assembly is grandly inaugurated and the Garden of Enlightenment is widely opened. The destiny of the nation rises in tandem with the destiny of the Buddha, and the imperial wind fans forth alongside the patriarchal wind.
Just as it is said that the old year has passed and the new year has arrived, I wonder: where does that which departs go?

"From where does it come? Such commentary becomes increasingly convoluted and erroneous. I dare ask the assembly: Within the single stroke beneath the patched robe, is there any increase or decrease, any coming or going?
After a long silence, he said: "The winter ends and the warmth returns; the shadowless tree flourishes.

Spring comes and the flowers bloom on the sproutless branch. He ascended the hall and said: "In the fifth month, the hibiscus flowers shine brightly before the eyes; the fragrant breeze and warbling birds pervade everywhere."
The stone door is closed. A single move ahead of the mechanism contains no mystery or subtlety. One must most certainly avoid recognizing color and sound as the person themselves.
Recall how Chan Master Heshan Shouduan addressed the assembly: "There is no dharma before the eyes; the meaning lies before the eyes.
It is not a dharma of the present moment; it is beyond the reach of ears and eyes. Tiantong Ju said: "Old man Heshan untied the sack and brought forth a rare treasure."
"Various treasures have been scattered before all the people. At such a time as this, what further is there to do?
When the road has no lost articles to be picked up, the gentleman praises it. The Master said, "The insights of both teachers, when scrutinized one by one, are entirely full of leaks.
Fengshan would not put it that way. If one perceives form or seeks sound, it is not the family treasure. He finished.
Know that before one’s eyes there is not a single dharma; head to head, object to object, all are in perfect resonance. If this is not yet so, listen further to the final phrase:
"When the Way prevails, the Son of Heaven does not issue commands; when the times are clear, one need not sing songs of peace.

When Emperor Taizong ascended the throne, the Master was commissioned by imperial decree to go to Japan to proclaim the sacred transformation. In the second year [of his reign], he returned with the officials of the mission. [The account is] complete.

The memorial was presented, and the Emperor was greatly pleased; his favor and patronage increased even further. In the sixth year, an imperial decree was issued to establish a Great Universal Salvation Retreat (Pudu Dazhaihui) at Mount Zhongshan, and the Master was commanded to ascend the seat and preach the Dharma; those who listened numbered tens of thousands.

In the eleventh year, he entered the capital for an audience with the Emperor and again received an imperial decree to hold a retreat at Daqingshou Monastery, where the gifts bestowed upon him were even more generous. In the third year of the Xuande era, the Master submitted a memorial on account of his old age.

He requested leave to return to the mountains. The Emperor took pity on him and dispatched an inner court official to escort him back south to the Western Hermitage (Xī Ān) in Tianjie to live out his final years.
On the eighth day of the twelfth month of the seventh year, he manifested slight illness; bidding farewell to the assembly, he recited a verse and passed away while sitting in the lotus posture.

Upon hearing the news, the Emperor dispatched an eunuch to present offerings, for which a written memorial exists. His secular age was eighty-one, and his monastic seniority (śrāmaṇera-vaṣa) was seventy-five. During his cremation, the smoke and flames [formed five-colored clouds].

As for the physical remains: a crane soared through the sky and a rare fragrance wafted ethereally. The officials, the nobility, the fourfold assembly, and ten thousand people all marveled at such a rarity.
The *śarīra* relics were round and red in countless numbers. By imperial decree, a stupa was constructed at Juefeng Chan Temple.
Chan Master Xichan of Tianqing Monastery in the Western Capital, whose dharma heir was Chan Master Xiang-an Yirang, was the son of the Li family in Zhending Prefecture.

Having shaved his head at the age of seven, he received full ordination and traveled extensively to consult various masters. Finally, he went to Fenglong Mountain to study under Guyan, who, upon seeing him at first glance, immediately praised him.
Later, he appeared in the world at Tianqing Temple. Subsequently, he moved to Kongxiang on Mount Xiong’er, Lingyan on Mount Tai, and Songshao in Luoyang.
In the summer of the Gengchen year, he fell ill and said to his disciples, "I shall not recover from this illness; you must prepare a stupa for me."
On the twelfth day of the fifth month, the construction of the stupa was completed. The Master gave instructions for his final affairs and then wrote this verse:
"When coming, it was originally pure; when departing, it is likewise perfect and complete. The void performs a dance, wandering freely at will. He then passed away lying on his right side.
The twenty-eighth generation descendant of Dajian (Baizhang),
Chan Master Songting Ziyen of Wannian in Nanyang Prefecture,
was a successor of Chan Master Shaoshi Cai. He was a native of Guishi County in Henan, and his clan name was Fan.
In his youth, he suffered frequently from illness; his parents, fearing he would not survive, sent him to follow Jiyun at Shaolin to receive instruction.

At eighteen, he received full ordination. By nature, the Master was exceptionally gifted and proficient in both Buddhist and secular classics. He first visited Jiang Yuezhao, then saw Xianan Rang, and later studied under Chunzhu Cai.
When Zhuan showed him the *Precious Mirror Samādhi* (*Baoming Sanmei*), the Master questioned and debated it repeatedly until his doubts were completely dispelled.
[The Master] said, "Obstructed. Zuó remarked, "To shoulder the Great Dharma rests entirely upon your person. He bestowed a verse which contained the lines: "A lion cub atop Wǔrù Peak;
illuminating the past and shining upon the future, it naturally transcends the crowd. At that time, the seat at Wàn'ān was vacant, and the fourfold assembly requested the Master to preside over it.
In the second year of the Hongwǔ era (Jǐyǒu), he moved to Shàoshì. He labored in the fields to provide for the community, composing a verse that said: "Returning after the chaos..."
From Nüyun: My life’s hardships, with whom can I speak? By day I pick up clods of earth to drive away mountain birds;
by night I sleep in a nest-like hut to chase off wild pigs. My heart breaks as the autumn wind frequently strikes the watch-tower gongs; my eyes gaze at the night moon until my soul is consumed.
Only in recent years have I come to know the bitterness of the farmer; even for a single meal, I still think of the benefactor’s kindness. The Winter of the Thirteenth Year at Zhouwang Hall.
Later, for the sake of the Empress Dowager Cixiao, the mother of the state, he was commanded to ascend the seat and preach the Dharma.
The Emperor bestowed upon him a *saṃghāṭī* robe to honor him. Subsequently, he lived in retirement due to old age.
Zen Master Xiong’er Songxi Ziding was a dharma successor of Zen Master Tianqing Rang. He was the son of Ma of Yan’er. At the age of seven, he followed Guruan to receive the tonsure.
When Guruan passed away, he went to visit Xianan, who appointed him as the library keeper. One day, while reporting on matters in the master’s quarters, [Xianan] spoke, and upon hearing these words—
He attained great enlightenment. After he took up residence, his governance of the assembly was stern and majestic, as chilling as autumn frost.

One day, manifesting a slight illness, he said to the assembly, "My worldly karmic conditions have come to an end; the time has arrived. You all must not harbor attachments through emotional consciousness.
Listen as I deliver the final word. After a long silence, he lay upon his pillow and passed away in stillness.
Chan Master Nengran Liaogui of Shaoshi on Mount Song was a dharma heir of Chan Master Wanan Yan, the twenty-ninth generation descendant of Dajian.
He was born into a prominent clan of Jindian in Songyang. From his childhood...

From his youth, he focused his mindfulness on the school of Emptiness (*śūnyatā*) and subsequently took refuge at Shaolin. At the age of twenty, he first donned the monastic robes. Initially, he visited Yueyin at Xiangshan;

having heard that Songting was propagating the Way at Tianqing Monastery, he went there to study under him. One day, as Songtong ascended the hall, he declared: "A single word transcends all, standing alone and peerless in its time.
Upon hearing these words, the Master attained sudden and complete liberation. He then returned to live in seclusion at the Second Patriarch’s [Baizhang] monastery.
An. In the twenty-third year of the Hongwu era, as the ancestral seat at the temple was vacant, the entire mountain community made a formal request for the Master to assume the position.

He declined with all his might, but being unable to refuse, he finally consented. Upon ascending the hall, he said: "Do not seek the standard within words; you must clarify the essence beyond the phrase.

If you can do so, you will penetrate the past and encompass the present, attaining spontaneous and unimpeded freedom. Do you understand? In the nineteenth year of the Yongle era, he suddenly gathered the assembly.
He took his final leave and spoke again in verse: "At eighty-seven years of age, I have come out at evening and entered again at evening.
Casting off my hands beyond the limit of awe-inspiring sound (*vīcī-śabda*), I am continuous and dense; I pass away in profound stillness."
Chan Master Qikong of Shaoshi on Mount Song,
a successor of Chan Master Gaizhi of Shaoshi in the thirtieth generation after Dajian, was a native of Yuqu County in Pingyang Prefecture. He went to attend upon Ningran.

He was shown the essentials of the mind, which he consulted and questioned day and night. One day, upon seeing a cypress tree planted by the Qin dynasty, he attained sudden and complete enlightenment.
He went straight to the master’s quarters; as soon as he saw him, the master suddenly said, "Qiyin has realized Chan. The profound essence of the Dongshan school rests within your person."
In the fourth year of the Jingtai era, he succeeded [his predecessor] as abbot. A monk asked, "What is the matter prior to the empty kalpa?
The Master replied, "A tortoise warming itself by the fire.
He was the thirty-first generation descendant of Dajian.
Chan Master Wufang Cancong of Dingguo Monastery in the Western Capital was a dharma successor of Chan Master Shaoshi Bin. He was the son of the Xu family of Luoyang.

He received the tonsure at Fuxian Pifeng Monastery. Initially, he visited Chaohua Zong and entered the inner chamber to seek instruction, gaining realization. Later, he went to Shaoshi to call upon Master Ju.

Kongshi revealed to him the subtle and profound depths of the teaching, but the Master was at a loss for what to do. One day, while casually examining the *Chuan Deng Lu* (Record of the Transmission of the Lamp), he encountered the account of how Tianyi called out to five practitioners simultaneously, beginning with "Venerable Shi.
Thereupon, he intuitively grasped the profound essence of the Five Ranks (*wuwei*) and immediately received formal certification (*inkan*).
He resided at Dingguo Temple in Guairuo. Later, in the sixth month of the tenth year of the Chenghua era, he manifested his passing. His lifespan was sixty...
With fourteen years of monastic seniority and forty years of life, he was interred at the ancestral tomb on Mount Shaoshi.
He was the Dharma heir of Chan Master Cong of Dingguo, the thirty-second generation descendant of Dajian.
Chan Master Wencai of Shaoji on Mount Song was a native of Tongzhou. His lineage was that of the Wang family of Guangning in Weizhou.
His grandfather, named Cai, served as a Military Merit General (*Wude Jiangjun*) under Emperor Taizong during the suppression of the internal rebellion; he subsequently settled in Tongzhou.
The Master’s mother dreamed of a monk seeking lodging, and upon waking, she conceived him. He received the tonsure and ordination from Master Ba’an Kong of Wan’an.

I went to Wulin to receive my full ordination robes; upon my return, I immediately closed my retreat quarters. While reading the *Niantiti* (Selections and Excerpts) by Wansong regarding the karmic encounters of ancient masters, I remained like someone facing a blank wall for a long time.
Suddenly, I attained an awakening and said: "The school of Caodong has spread its style throughout the world with the skill of 'woven palindrome' embroidery (*zhijin huíwén*).
Were it not for the density of the needlework and the intricate, winding interplay that avoids hitting the head-on point, no one could fathom it."
He bestowed [the Dharma] upon him. Subsequently, he passed through the pass to attend upon Master Wufangqin; after relying on him for a long time, he received the seal of transmission.

In the first year of the Zhengde era, he resided at Shaoshi. Ascending the hall, he said: "The West-coming Dharma Master [Bodhidharma] transmitted the Single Vehicle Dharma directly and simply, enabling people to see their nature and become Buddhas.
Its arrival here at Shaoshi is like nine tripods suspended from a single thread. You all must seize the opportunity while the color [of the thread] remains."
His strength was robust. To accomplish this matter, you must exert yourself with all your might; do not let the days pass in vain.
In the third year of the Jiajing era (1524), the year of Jia-shen, when the Master was seventy years old, he retired to dwell among the Thirty-six Peaks.

The thirty-third generation descendant of Dajian (Baizhang), Chan Master Xiaozhi of Shaoshi, was succeeded by Chan Master Zongshu of Mount Xiao at Beijing Zongjing. He was the son of the Li family of Nanhui in Shunde. From [himself]...
From childhood he was unlike ordinary children; whenever he played, he would invariably perform Buddhist rites. When he was over ten years old, he had already mastered the classics and histories.

One day, he suddenly closed his books and sighed, saying, "This is not the Dharma for transcending the world. He then took leave of his parents and went to the Kaiyuan Temple in his village to shave his head.
Hearing of the flourishing reputation of Yuezhou’s dharma assembly, he went to visit him and remained in his service for eight years, receiving his instruction intimately.
Only then did he receive formal certification (*kanna*). In the thirty-sixth year of the Jiajing era, when the Master was requested to take up residence at Mount Xiao Shi, he sighed and said:
"More than thirty years have passed since the passing of my late teacher, and the Cao-Dong school is on the verge of extinction. As a predecessor once said:
'In the declining age of the Zen groves, those who propagate the Dharma often seek a life of ease and do not urgently provide support. Before long, its collapse will be imminent.'"

Although he felt ashamed at being entrusted with such a charge, how could he refuse the entrustment? He thus took charge of it. At that time, a severe drought prevailed and the rivers and wells had run dry;

when the Master arrived at the source of a spring, it surged once more. In the year Bingyin, he moved to Zongjing. In the first year of the Longqing era, he traveled to Sanxue Cave in the Western Mountains;
finding it secluded and profound, he settled there. When winter arrived, he suddenly manifested a slight illness. On the sixteenth day of the twelfth lunar month—
He took up his brush and wrote a verse, saying: "Mirror of the Source, Mirror of the Source! When the mind-dharma becomes practice, one realizes perfect enlightenment this very day;
when the mirror is broken, the source is rectified. Having finished writing, he sat upright and passed away. His secular age was sixty-eight, and his years as a monk were fifty-six.
His remains were cremated and divided into three parts, and stupas were erected for them at Zongjing (the Mirror of the Source), Shunde, and Shaoshi.
The thirty-fourth generation descendant of Dajian [Huineng],
Chan Master Daqianhuanyou Changrun of Shaoshi in the Western Capital (Luoyang),
a successor of Chan Master Zongjing Shu, was the son of the Huang family of Jinxian in Nanchang. From his youth...
At that time, while watching a performance of a mixed-style drama, he was moved by a deep realization. He subsequently went to Mount Funiu to follow Tanyanping and receive the tonsure.

After three years there, he remained utterly bewildered and at a loss for what to do; his doubts could not be resolved through questioning. He then traveled south to Mount Jing to pay his respects to Wansong, where he surrendered himself in sincerity to seek instruction.
Song said, "I wonder who it is that has placed this thing here. The Master became increasingly perplexed and dejected. He then went to listen to a lecture on the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*.

Upon reaching the passage, "The perfect, clear, and knowing awareness does not depend on mental thought," he suddenly attained realization. He then went to see Daofang of Lian and asked, "When a reflection suddenly appears in a mirror, what should be done?
Fang replied, "You must simply smash it to pieces. The Master did not find this satisfactory, so he returned to consult Xiaoyun.
Sansheng brought up the previous conversation. Sansheng said, "Why must you break it? The Master said, "What can be done about the reflections in the mirror?
Sansheng said, "Where are the reflections right now? Try bringing them out for me to see. At that moment, the Master was suddenly relieved and became even more resolute.
One day, in the meditation hall, Sansheng brought up Dongshan’s saying, "I am not he now," and asked the Master, "Since you are not he..."
"In the end, who is this? The Master, having received the intent, presented a verse, saying: "If you wish to recognize this person, there is a true message:
Formless, he fills the void; With form, he leaves no trace. He has been the teacher of Buddhas and patriarchs; He constantly serves as the standard for humans and devas.
From a whisk of tortoise hair, a pure breeze arises; From the tip of a staff of hare horns, the bright moon emerges. Yunmen said, "My son, do not plagiarize."
[The Master] said, "You must further enter the gate of awakening yourself. The Master said, "If you do not even rely on conditions, through what gate would one enter?
Shanshan said, "Since you do not rely on conditions, for what reason have you come here? The Master said, "Precisely because I do not rely on conditions, I have come here.
Shanshan said, "Regarding the phrase 'not relying on conditions,' what is its meaning? The Master said, "A colorful phoenix soars and flies with body at ease; [iron...]"
Niu Benhou’s mind was always at ease. Mount Shan said, “Excellent. The next day, he took his leave. Mount Shan bestowed upon him a verse containing the lines:
“One who has attained stability shall become a lord of men; you should contemplate the autumn of Shaoshi. The Master said, “What kind of person am I that I would dare to accept such words?”
Master Shan further entrusted him, saying, "The Way has long been in decline; how can one simply fold one's hands and do nothing? The Master responded with repeated acquiescence.

When Master Shan passed away, the community deliberated that none but the Master was fit to serve as abbot. The Master declined the honor three times, but the assembly then cited the words of Master Shan’s final entrustment to urge him on.
The Master suddenly shed tears and said no more, whereupon he took charge of the monastery affairs. This was during the second year of the Wanli era.

It was the autumn of the year Jiashu (1610). The Master’s physical presence was robust and dignified, and his voice was like a great bell. His character was broad and serene as he bore the Great Dharma upon his shoulders.
Morning and night he was diligent and never slackened for a moment. Among his disciples who entered his inner quarters were two hundred and seventy people.
On the twenty-seventh day of the fourth month in the thirteenth year of the Wanli era, he bid farewell to the assembly, wrote a verse, and passed away.
Chan Master Changzhong Yunkong of Lingshan in Jianchang Prefecture requested instruction on the essentials of the Dharma from Master Shouchang.
The Master said, "If you can be diligent and refuse to deceive yourself, this is the practice that penetrates from beginning to end.

One day, hearing a practitioner discussing the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, the Master rebuked him, saying, "If the eye of the school is not clear, how can it be the ultimate? Upon hearing this, Shouchang was utterly bewildered.
He lost his way and asked, "What is the Eye of the School? The Master shook out his robe and rose. Chang requested further instruction, to which the Master replied, "I truly do not know;
you must look for it yourself. Later, at Mount Dàhǎo, Chang attained enlightenment. He went to the master’s quarters to present what he had realized.
The Master said, "Your realization is indeed not without merit, but you must still ensure that its application is thorough before you can succeed. I fear it may be merely..."
Yao Hengyin Chan; the thirty-fifth generation descendant under Dajian (Dajian Huineng),
Dharma heir of Chan Master Xiaoshi Run.
Chan Master Fangnian of Beidajue Qingliang Cizhou was the son of the Yang family of Tangxian. At the age of ten, he followed Master Yigong of Guangde Daci in Jintai to undergo tonsure.

He received full ordination and traveled among lecture halls to investigate the essential principles of the *Dharmalakṣaṇa* (Nature-Characteristics) and *Dharmatā-lakṣaṇa* (True-Characteristics) schools.
One day, he abandoned his studies and departed, eventually traveling to Shaolin to visit Master Huanxiu. When Huanxiu asked, "Where have you come from? the Master replied, "From the North."
Fangxiu asked, "How does the Way of the Buddhas and Patriarchs in the north compare to that here?
The Master replied, "The waters divide into a thousand branches, yet they flow from a single source. Fangxiu found these words extraordinary and appointed him as the *weina*.

One day, while visiting the site where the First Patriarch sat facing a wall, he suddenly attained realization and said, "Before the Five Milk Peaks, what a marvelous message! Every single stone, large and small, bears it upon it."
Dishi went to the master’s chamber to present [the text] for his inspection. Xuefeng granted his seal of approval and instructed him, saying:
"From the Buddhas and Patriarchs of antiquity down to the present, they have transmitted one to another what they themselves have realized, desiring that all sentient beings know it exists.
I received it from my late teacher Xiaoshan; I now transmit it to you. You should take the mind of the Buddhas and Patriarchs as your own mind to continue the life of wisdom. Nevertheless—"

It was thus. Xu concealed his traces among the forests and springs, waiting for the right time to emerge. He was entrusted with a verse which said: "The unsurpassed mind of nirvana has been transmitted from Buddha to Patriarch;
now that the time for my transmission has come, the clouds have cleared and the peak reveals its summit. At that time, he was twenty-eight years old.
He then went to Mount Wutai to close himself in retreat, eating only once a day and not providing himself with bedding. Later, he proceeded to the East Terrace at the invitation of the assembly.

He suddenly lost his sight in both eyes. The Master said, "This illusory body is not subject to illness; from where could it have come? After practicing meditative concentration for seven days, his vision was restored.
Upon returning from his southern pilgrimage to Potalaka, he next stayed at Dashiensi in Yue. The assembly requested him to remain at Zhifengtu to preach the Dharma.
Zhanran Cheng came to study under him. The Master asked, "Zhifengtu is near the Green Mountains; by the side of the King’s City in Yue lies the vast blue sea."
"How is it at a distance? Zhenran replied, "The moon pierces the blue sea; the Persian does not knit his brows.
The Master further asked about the fundamental tenets of the Dongshan school. Zhenran presented this verse: "The five ranks of ruler and subject must be known intimately;

within them, why wait for thought? The stone woman is skilled at playing without needle or thread; the wooden puppet can pull the mechanism beyond transformation. Red dust rises from the bottom of the well."
Misty and vast, white waves surge and fly upon the mountain peaks. His birth was originally effortless; he unconsciously attained the natural imperial foundation.
The Master said, "His words and phrases are dense and subtle, falling neither into beginning nor end. He is truly a scion of our own house.
Hereafter, you shall have the capacity to cut off the tongues of all people under heaven. He then bestowed upon him a verse, saying: "A single drop from Caoxi..."
Water. The Buddhas and Patriarchs transmitted it to one another; even now, at the time of its transmission, the great earth becomes nectar.
*Tu!* At the peak of Wuyufeng, an unbarbed arrow struck down half a child from the south. In the year Renchen, he was invited by the monastics and laypeople of Jiaxing to reside at Dongta.
Subsequently, he accepted the invitation to Yunju. In the autumn of the twenty-second year of the Wanli era, the Jiawu year (1594), at Mount Wutai, the Ancient Qing.
The Special Envoy from Liang invited the Master to expound the Dharma; both the monastics and the laity earnestly requested him to remain. Before long, he manifested his passing.
His disciple Zhanran escorted his remains and enshrined them in a stupa on the southern mountain of Xiansheng Temple.
Chan Master Wuyan Zhengdao of Shaoshi on Mount Song was the son of the Hu family of Yuzhang. He entered the monastic order under Shanglan.

At the age of fifteen, he encountered the elder master Xiu, who recognized his potential and instructed him in the essentials of the Dharma. Subsequently, he followed Xiu to rest and practice at Jingping Rock on Mount Nanyue.
One day, Xiu said to the Master, "If you wish to investigate and clarify this matter, you must thread through the entanglements of both doctrine and tradition."
After some time, he was finally permitted to go and see Xuanzhan. Xuanzhan said to Xiu, "Wu'an is worthy of being called a vessel of the Dharma.
You must by no means obstruct his mind with your own partial knowledge and views; simply have him travel south to inquire for himself, so that he may realize it through his own self-reflection.

Xiu then brought up the verse by Zhang Zhuo to test the Master. The Master said, "Even True Suchness cannot be established as a thing; how could there be such a thing as a verse? Upon seeing this, Xiu [was convinced].
His faculties were sharp and keen. He was further commanded to attend Shao-shi (Mount Shaoshi) under Huanxiu.

One day, as Huan was ascending the hall for formal discourse, the Master stepped forward and asked, "What is the家风 (family style/tradition) of the Dongshan school? Huan replied, "Three blossoming trees beneath the moon; twin cassia branches before the peak.
The Master asked, "Does the Master have anything else besides this? Huan said, "There is only this one reality; there is neither a second nor a third. At these words, the Master attained realization.

Upon attaining great enlightenment, he presented a verse, saying: "Clouds gather at the mountain peak; The moon locks the secluded crag. The stone man claps his hands; The wooden woman smiles. Huanji then certified him with a verse, saying:
"The ineffable ultimate meaning does not depart from words; The profound chant and profound transmission are wondrously supreme.
Today, the single transmission is personally certified and bestowed; In years to come, the twin cassias shall benefit humans and devas. The 18th year of the Wanli era.
In the year of Gengyin, the Master presided over Shaoshi. A monk asked, "When the World-Honored One remained silent for a long time when asked neither about words nor non-words, what was his meaning?
The Master said, "To manifest the ancient path through one's demeanor is not to fall into the trap of a silent mechanism.

The monk asked, "What is the Buddha-dharma at the beginning of the new year? The Master held up his whisk and said, "Do you understand? The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Next year..."
There is yet another new branch here; there is no need for further repeated explanation. Once, an old master asked, "What is 'wordlessness'? The Master replied, "The four seasons proceed.
On another day, yet another old master asked, "What is 'wordlessness'? The Master replied, "The myriad things grow.
The Master’s functional ingenuity was swift and nimble, and his disposition was plain and sincere. Later, when he passed away, he was interred in the Patriarchal [Monastery].

Tomb Inscription for Chan Master Wuming Huijing of Shouchang in Jianchang Prefecture, Dharma Heir of Chan Master Zhong of Lingshan. He was the son of the Pei family of Chongren in Fuzhou. From birth...

He was exceptionally gifted and possessed a serene detachment, having no particular worldly preferences. At the age of nine, upon entering a local monastery, he immediately asked, "What is this 'vast and untrammeled spirit' (*vairāgya*)?
The master of the monastery marveled at his insight. When he grew up, he recited the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* as if recovering something long lost.

He then went to rely on Lingshan, where he constantly harbored doubts regarding the four-line verse. One day, he saw the verse by Master Fu (Bodhisattva Fotuo), which said: "If one were to discuss the four-line verse..."
It did not leave his body, yet he was unaware of its release. He composed a verse, saying:
"The four-line verse of the Vajra, Without shadow and without form, Originally not a single word— It radiates light throughout the entire world. At that time, he was twenty-four years old.

While casually perusing the Tripitaka, he reached the "Chapter on the Eye of the School" (*Zongyan pin*) and only then realized the principle of the "separate transmission outside the teachings. He subsequently took his leave of Linsan.
He thatched a hut at the summit of Mount E’feng and composed a verse, saying: *Treading upon the first peak above the clouds, The expanse before my eyes is wider than empty space.

At that time, I wished to see it but had no means to do so; Today we meet, and everywhere it is the same.* On another day, while examining the *Chuan Deng Lu* (Record of the Transmission of the Lamp), he saw a monk ask Xingshan, "What is the Way? Shan replied, "A magnificent mountain. The Master was perplexed by this.
He could not resolve it. Day and night he maintained his mindfulness, neglecting both sleep and food. While moving a stone, he found it so solid that it could not be lifted;
as he pushed with all his might, he suddenly attained great enlightenment. He composed a verse, saying: "If you wish to study the unsurpassed path of Bodhi, Hurry to clear away this great mountain.
Only when you know the Way do you realize the mountain is not good; Turn your body around and leap out of the Patriarch’s barrier. He went to present this to Lingquan.
"Mountain. Taking the mountain seal as his dharma-vessel, he first shaved his head and received full ordination at this time.
He remained within the mountains for another twenty-four years. In the *jiawu* year of the Wanli era, at age fifty-one, he finally emerged to reside at Baofang.
